### Step 1: Write failing tests for the aggregator

Create `tests/sequential-learning-aggregate.test.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * v1.7.5 -- multi-seed aggregation helpers. Pure math, no DB.
 */

import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import {
  mean, stdDev, ciHalfWidth95, aggregatePhases,
} from '../benchmarks/sequential-learning/aggregate.mjs';

describe('aggregate helpers (v1.7.5)', () => {
  it('mean of [0.1, 0.2, 0.3] = 0.2', () => {
    expect(mean([0.1, 0.2, 0.3])).toBeCloseTo(0.2, 5);
  });

  it('stdDev of identical values is 0', () => {
    expect(stdDev([0.5, 0.5, 0.5])).toBeCloseTo(0, 5);
  });

  it('ciHalfWidth95 for 10-sample [0.10..0.20] ≈ 0.0315 (t-crit 2.262 / sqrt(10))', () => {
    // Hand-verified: mean=0.15, var=0.0175/9≈0.001944, sd≈0.04410,
    // CI = 2.262 * 0.04410 / sqrt(10) ≈ 0.0315 (NOT 0.026 — that was wrong in plan v1).
    expect(ciHalfWidth95([0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.15])).toBeCloseTo(0.032, 2);
  });

  it('ciHalfWidth95 returns 0 for n=1 (no sample variance estimable)', () => {
    expect(ciHalfWidth95([0.5])).toBe(0);
  });

  it('ciHalfWidth95 rejects samples below n=5 by returning 0 (codex P2 — n=2/3/4 t-crit gives nonsense CI)', () => {
    expect(ciHalfWidth95([0.5, 0.6])).toBe(0);
    expect(ciHalfWidth95([0.5, 0.6, 0.7])).toBe(0);
    expect(ciHalfWidth95([0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8])).toBe(0);
    // n=5 is the floor where CI is reportable
    expect(ciHalfWidth95([0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5])).toBe(0); // zero variance still works
  });

  it('aggregatePhases averages early/mid/late across seeds', () => {
    const seeds = [
      { early: 0.80, mid: 0.20, late: 0.10 },
      { early: 0.70, mid: 0.30, late: 0.15 },
      { early: 0.75, mid: 0.25, late: 0.05 },
    ];
    const agg = aggregatePhases(seeds);
    expect(agg.early.mean).toBeCloseTo(0.75, 5);
    expect(agg.mid.mean).toBeCloseTo(0.25, 5);
    expect(agg.late.mean).toBeCloseTo(0.10, 5);
    expect(agg.late.ci95).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});
```

Run: `npx vitest run tests/sequential-learning-aggregate.test.ts`
Expected: FAIL — `aggregate.mjs` does not exist.

### Step 2: Implement `aggregate.mjs`

```js
// benchmarks/sequential-learning/aggregate.mjs
// v1.7.5 -- pure aggregation helpers for multi-seed runs. No imports beyond
// Node built-ins. Keep this file dependency-free so the benchmark runs on a
// vanilla Node 22+ install.

export function mean(xs) {
  if (xs.length === 0) return 0;
  return xs.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / xs.length;
}

export function stdDev(xs) {
  if (xs.length < 2) return 0;
  const m = mean(xs);
  const sumSq = xs.reduce((a, b) => a + (b - m) ** 2, 0);
  return Math.sqrt(sumSq / (xs.length - 1)); // sample stddev
}

// t-distribution critical values for 95% two-sided, df = n - 1.
// Hardcoded for n in [2..30]; falls back to 1.960 (z) for n > 30.
const T_CRIT_95 = {
  2: 12.706, 3: 4.303, 4: 3.182, 5: 2.776, 6: 2.571, 7: 2.447,
  8: 2.365, 9: 2.306, 10: 2.262, 11: 2.228, 12: 2.201, 13: 2.179,
  14: 2.160, 15: 2.145, 16: 2.131, 17: 2.120, 18: 2.110, 19: 2.101,
  20: 2.093, 21: 2.086, 22: 2.080, 23: 2.074, 24: 2.069, 25: 2.064,
  26: 2.060, 27: 2.056, 28: 2.052, 29: 2.048, 30: 2.045,
};

export function ciHalfWidth95(xs) {
  // v1.7.5 codex P2 -- reject n<5 by returning 0. n=2 t-crit=12.706 gives
  // nonsense CIs; eval requires n>=10 anyway. Smoke runs labelled
  // exploratory, no CI reported.
  if (xs.length < 5) return 0;
  const t = T_CRIT_95[xs.length] ?? 1.960;
  return (t * stdDev(xs)) / Math.sqrt(xs.length);
}

/**
 * v1.7.5 -- exact paired permutation CI for mean(deltaA - deltaB).
 * Used in Task 3 instead of paired t-test: phase rates are bounded
 * binomial-like and t-test is fragile at n=20. Permutation makes no
 * normality assumption.
 *
 * @param {number[]} xsA per-seed late-rate for condition A
 * @param {number[]} xsB per-seed late-rate for condition B (same seeds)
 * @param {number} alpha 0.05 for 95% CI
 * @param {number} nResamples e.g. 10_000
 * @returns {{deltaMean: number, ciLow: number, ciHigh: number}}
 */
export function pairedPermutationCI(xsA, xsB, alpha = 0.05, nResamples = 10_000) {
  if (xsA.length !== xsB.length) throw new Error('pairedPermutationCI: lengths differ');
  const n = xsA.length;
  if (n < 5) throw new Error('pairedPermutationCI: n<5');
  const diffs = xsA.map((a, i) => a - xsB[i]);
  const observed = mean(diffs);

  // Sign-flip permutation: each resample flips signs randomly, then re-means.
  // Use mulberry32 internally so this is deterministic given a seed env.
  const rng = mulberry32(0x9E3779B9);
  const resampledMeans = [];
  for (let r = 0; r < nResamples; r++) {
    let s = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) s += diffs[i] * (rng() < 0.5 ? -1 : 1);
    resampledMeans.push(s / n);
  }
  // Bias-corrected percentile bounds around the observed mean.
  resampledMeans.sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const loIdx = Math.floor((alpha / 2) * nResamples);
  const hiIdx = Math.ceil((1 - alpha / 2) * nResamples) - 1;
  const ciLow = observed + (resampledMeans[loIdx] - mean(resampledMeans));
  const ciHigh = observed + (resampledMeans[hiIdx] - mean(resampledMeans));
  return { deltaMean: observed, ciLow, ciHigh };
}

// mulberry32 lives here so aggregate.mjs has a deterministic RNG dep-free.
function mulberry32(seed) {
  let s = seed >>> 0;
  return function () {
    s = (s + 0x6D2B79F5) >>> 0;
    let t = s;
    t = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1);
    t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61);
    return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  };
}

/**
 * Aggregate a list of per-seed phase rates into mean/stddev/CI per phase.
 * @param {Array<{early: number, mid: number, late: number}>} seedResults
 * @returns {{early: {mean, std, ci95}, mid: {...}, late: {...}}}
 */
export function aggregatePhases(seedResults) {
  const result = {};
  for (const phase of ['early', 'mid', 'late']) {
    const xs = seedResults.map((r) => r[phase]);
    result[phase] = { mean: mean(xs), std: stdDev(xs), ci95: ciHalfWidth95(xs) };
  }
  return result;
}
```

### Step 3: Add seeded RNG + MEANINGFUL variance to `traps.mjs`

**Reviewer finding:** Plan v1's "shuffle within thirds" was MISCONCEIVED — `traps.mjs` already places traps at fixed positions (e.g. `bare_except` at 4, 28, 46), so within-thirds shuffling only reshuffles trap-vs-clean positions (clean = no-op). The "seed" varies almost nothing real and CIs would be artificially tiny.

**Real seed variance source (chosen):** Randomly assign WHICH category appears at each trap-slot within each phase bucket, while preserving (a) the slot positions themselves (early/mid/late distribution unchanged), (b) the count of trap encounters per category (each category still appears 2-3 times across the sequence), (c) the early-then-later structure (each category's first encounter is in early or mid, second in mid or late, third if any in late).

Implementation:

```js
// v1.7.5 -- mulberry32 RNG, dep-free.
function mulberry32(seed) { /* same as aggregate.mjs */ }

/**
 * Deterministic Fisher-Yates shuffle scoped to an index list.
 * @param {number[]} arr indices to shuffle in place
 */
function shuffleIndices(arr, rng) {
  for (let i = arr.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
    const j = Math.floor(rng() * (i + 1));
    [arr[i], arr[j]] = [arr[j], arr[i]];
  }
  return arr;
}

/**
 * Generate the 50-task sequence, optionally with seed-driven category-to-slot
 * randomization. Seed varies WHICH category lands at each trap slot within
 * each phase bucket. Preserves: total trap count, slot positions, per-category
 * encounter count, early-then-later structure.
 *
 * @param {number} [seed] - integer; same seed produces identical output
 */
export function generateTasks(seed) {
  // 1. Build the canonical fixed-position structure: { earlySlots: [pos...],
  //    midSlots: [pos...], lateSlots: [pos...] } from the existing TRAPS
  //    array (which encodes category -> [pos1, pos2, pos3]).
  // 2. For each phase bucket, collect (category, encounter_index) pairs that
  //    land in that phase. Shuffle the assignment of pairs to slots within
  //    the phase using mulberry32(seedForPhase). Each phase uses its own
  //    sub-seed derived from `seed` to avoid correlated streams across phases.
  // 3. Re-emit the 50-task array with the new (slot, category) assignments.
  // 4. Filler positions (no trap) stay filler.

  if (typeof seed !== 'number') {
    return generateCanonicalTasks(); // existing fixed ordering
  }

  // codex P2 -- hash-derive sub-seeds to avoid correlation across phases.
  const earlyRng = mulberry32((0x9E3779B9 * (seed + 1)) >>> 0);
  const midRng   = mulberry32((0x9E3779B9 * (seed + 2)) >>> 0);
  const lateRng  = mulberry32((0x9E3779B9 * (seed + 3)) >>> 0);

  // ... assign categories to slots per phase using each rng ...
  // (full implementation reads TRAPS structure + emits tasks array)
}
```

**Pre-flight before writing this code:** read `benchmarks/sequential-learning/traps.mjs` in full to understand the canonical TRAPS structure (likely `{ id, tags, lesson, recallQueries[] }` per category, plus an array mapping category to fixed positions). The category-to-slot algorithm depends on this exact shape.

**Determinism + variance tests** in `tests/sequential-learning-aggregate.test.ts`:

```ts
it('generateTasks(seed) is deterministic for a given seed', () => {
  const a = generateTasks(42);
  const b = generateTasks(42);
  expect(a).toEqual(b);
});

it('generateTasks(seed) varies meaningfully across different seeds', () => {
  // Same number of trap tasks (deterministic structure preserved)
  const s1 = generateTasks(1000);
  const s2 = generateTasks(1001);
  const trapCount1 = s1.filter((t) => t.trapCategory).length;
  const trapCount2 = s2.filter((t) => t.trapCategory).length;
  expect(trapCount1).toBe(trapCount2);
  // But which category lands at each trap position differs at >half the slots
  const trapPositions = s1.map((t, i) => (t.trapCategory ? i : null)).filter((i) => i !== null);
  let differingSlots = 0;
  for (const i of trapPositions) {
    if (s1[i].trapCategory !== s2[i].trapCategory) differingSlots++;
  }
  expect(differingSlots).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(Math.floor(trapPositions.length / 2));
});

it('generateTasks(seed) preserves per-category encounter count', () => {
  const tasks = generateTasks(42);
  const byCat = {};
  for (const t of tasks) {
    if (t.trapCategory) byCat[t.trapCategory] = (byCat[t.trapCategory] ?? 0) + 1;
  }
  // each category still appears 2-3 times (verified against canonical TRAPS)
  for (const [cat, count] of Object.entries(byCat)) {
    expect(count).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
    expect(count).toBeLessThanOrEqual(3);
  }
});

it('generateTasks(seed) preserves early-then-later structure', () => {
  // For each category, first encounter must be in positions 0-16 (early third).
  const tasks = generateTasks(42);
  const firstSeen = {};
  tasks.forEach((t, i) => {
    if (t.trapCategory && firstSeen[t.trapCategory] === undefined) {
      firstSeen[t.trapCategory] = i;
    }
  });
  for (const pos of Object.values(firstSeen)) {
    expect(pos).toBeLessThan(17); // each category first-encountered in early third
  }
});
```

**Stop condition:** If reading `traps.mjs` reveals the canonical TRAPS structure does NOT support the assignment algorithm (e.g., categories' fixed positions intertwine in a way that prevents per-phase reassignment), STOP and report. The seed variance plan needs a different shape.

### Step 4: Add `--seed` and `--n-seeds` to `run.mjs`

```js
function parseArgs() {
  const args = process.argv.slice(2);
  const opts = {
    adapter: 'all',
    output: join(__dirname, 'results'),
    useGoalStack: false,
    seed: undefined,
    nSeeds: 1,
  };
  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
    if (args[i] === '--adapter' && args[i + 1]) opts.adapter = args[++i];
    else if (args[i] === '--output' && args[i + 1]) opts.output = args[++i];
    else if (args[i] === '--use-goal-stack') opts.useGoalStack = true;
    else if (args[i] === '--seed' && args[i + 1]) opts.seed = parseInt(args[++i], 10);
    else if (args[i] === '--n-seeds' && args[i + 1]) opts.nSeeds = parseInt(args[++i], 10);
    // ...
  }
  return opts;
}
```

Multi-seed loop in `runAdapter` (or wherever the per-adapter run lives):

```js
async function runAdapter(name, adapter, opts) {
  const seeds = opts.nSeeds > 1
    ? Array.from({ length: opts.nSeeds }, (_, i) => 1000 + i)
    : [opts.seed ?? 0];
  const seedResults = [];
  for (const seed of seeds) {
    const tasks = generateTasks(seed);
    const results = await simulate(adapter, tasks, { useGoalStack: opts.useGoalStack });
    seedResults.push({ seed, phases: phaseRates(results), overall: trapHitRate(results) });
  }
  const phaseAgg = aggregatePhases(seedResults.map((r) => r.phases));
  return { name, seedResults, phaseAgg };
}
```

Output JSON shape:

{
  "benchmark": "hippo-sequential-learning",
  "version": "1.7.5",
  "config": { "useGoalStack": true, "nSeeds": 10 },
  "conditions": {
    "hippo": {
      "seeds": [{ "seed": 1000, "phases": {...}, "overall": 0.30 }, ...],
      "phaseAggregate": { "early": {"mean": ..., "std": ..., "ci95": ...}, ... }
    }
  }
}
```

### Step 1: Write the pre-registration doc

Create `docs/evals/2026-05-07-v1.7.5-goal-stack-eval-prereg.md`:

```markdown
# v1.7.5 Goal-Stack Eval — Pre-Registration

**Pre-registered:** 2026-05-07, BEFORE running the eval.
**Author:** Keith So
**Mechanism under test:** B3 dlPFC goal-stack boost (v0.38.0 ship; v1.7.4 lift into shared helper).
**Public claim being tested:** Goal-stack provides ≥10pp ADDITIONAL drop in late-phase trap-hit-rate on top of base hippo (78% → 14% baseline). Source of claim: TODOS.md v0.39.0 B3 follow-ups, plus general references in CHANGELOG/RESEARCH.md.

## Protocol

- Benchmark: `benchmarks/sequential-learning` (v1.7.5 multi-seed harness with category-to-slot variance).
- **Conditions (4, not 2):**
  - **C0 — none:** `baseline` adapter, no memory.
  - **C1 — static:** `static` adapter, all lessons pre-loaded.
  - **C2 — hippo-base:** `hippo` adapter, `--use-goal-stack` OFF.
  - **C3 — hippo+goalstack:** `hippo` adapter, `--use-goal-stack` ON.
- **Seeds: 20.** Hash-derived (`0x9E3779B9 * (1000+i) >>> 0` for i in 0..19) to avoid correlated mulberry32 streams.
- **Eval mode:** `--eval-strict` flag → simulator hard-fails on any pushGoal/completeGoal hook error. Hook-failure counts written to result JSON; non-zero counts disqualify the run.
- **Primary metric (PRE-LOCKED):** late-phase trap-hit-rate. **"Late" definition (PRE-LOCKED):** positions 34-49 inclusive (last third, 0-indexed). Measured per seed by counting `trapHit === true` among trap-tasks at those positions, divided by trap-task count at those positions.
- **Top-5 cap interaction (PRE-LOCKED):** a task is "trap hit" iff `isRecalled(top5, category) === false`. The top-5 cap is part of the metric definition; right-lesson-at-rank-6 counts as a hit, by design.
- **Reporting:** mean ± 95% CI per phase, per condition. Plus paired Δ (C2 vs C3) via permutation CI.

## Statistical method (PRE-LOCKED)

- **Estimand:** mean late-phase Δ in percentage points = `mean_late(C2) − mean_late(C3)` over the 20 paired seeds.
- **CI method:** exact paired sign-flip permutation, 10,000 resamples (`pairedPermutationCI` in `aggregate.mjs`). NOT t-test — phase rates are bounded discrete and t-test is fragile at n=20 with binomial-like variance.
- **Robustness check:** Wilcoxon signed-rank p-value reported alongside (informational; primary CI is permutation).

## Decision rule (mechanical)

- **Δ ≥ 0.10 AND lower permutation-CI bound > 0** → **DEMONSTRATED.** Ship with "DEMONSTRATED" template.
- **Δ < 0.10 OR CI overlaps 0** → **RETRACTED.** Ship with "RETRACTED" template. Apply the retraction sweep below to ALL claim locations.
- **Δ < 0 (goal-stack HARMS performance)** → **RETRACTED + flag for v1.8 followup.** Mechanism may need design review before further use.
- **Any condition fails to run cleanly** (seed crash, hook failure, baseline drift) → STOP, fix, re-run. No partial-data ship.

## Stop conditions (mid-run)

- If C2 (hippo-base) late-phase mean diverges from README headline by >±10pp (i.e. >24% or <4%): harness is broken or headline is stale. STOP, investigate before scoring C3.
- If any seed crashes in any condition: drop that seed across ALL conditions (paired) and run a replacement seed with index 1020+. Do NOT cherry-pick.
- If `hookFailures.push > 0` or `hookFailures.complete > 0` in C3: the run is contaminated. STOP, fix, restart. (eval-strict mode prevents partial completions reaching the aggregator.)
- If any single seed's late-phase rate is >3 stddev from the rest in either condition: investigate (FS error, network blip, etc.). Drop or include based on investigation; document the choice.

## Risk register

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|------------|
| **Boost mechanism doesn't fire — eval RETRACTS for the wrong reason** (P0 from outside-voice review) | High (was the dominant P0) | `simulate()` stores memories with `[category.id, ...category.tags, 'error']` so the goal name `category.id` matches a real tag. Task 1 success criteria includes a smoke assertion that `goal_recall_log` has rows after a smoke run. STOP if zero rows. |
| **Seed variance is statistical theatre** (within-thirds shuffle was misconceived) | High (was P0) | Real variance source: random assignment of CATEGORIES to position-slots within each phase. Determinism + variance + per-category-encounter-count + early-then-later tests pin the algorithm. |
| Single deterministic run produces a number; we publish "10pp lift" without statistical defensibility | High (prior pattern) | Multi-seed harness mandatory. Pre-registered decision rule. BOTH templates pre-committed. |
| Confirmation bias — running the eval, wanting a positive result | High (human nature) | Pre-registered decision rule + claim-inventory artifact committed BEFORE eval. Decision mechanical. |
| HIPPO_HOME / XDG_DATA_HOME isolation hole — eval contaminates real store | Medium (codex P0) | Adapter sets `HIPPO_HOME=<temp>` and clears `XDG_DATA_HOME` in child env. Pre-flight grep verifies precedence. |
| Hook failures swallow silently — eval looks null but boost never fired | Medium (codex P1) | `--eval-strict` mode + finally cleanup + nonzero hookFailures aborts. Sanity gate post-run. |
| Paired t-test fragile for bounded discrete rates at n=20 | Medium (codex P1) | `pairedPermutationCI` (exact sign-flip, 10k resamples) is the primary CI. Wilcoxon signed-rank as robustness check. No t-test. |
| Late-phase has only ~7-9 trap encounters per seed → coarse 14pp steps | Medium (senior P1) | N=20 (not 10). Document residual variance clearly in the result doc. |
| Confounding — goal-stack adds CLI calls; differential overhead bias | Low | Paired-on-same-seed A/B controls for it. Permutation CI requires no further assumption. |
| Subprocess overhead inflates wall time | Low | Smoke first. Time budget accounts for ~15-20 min total. |
| Eval reveals goal-stack is HARMFUL (Δ < 0) | Low | Pre-reg has explicit "Δ < 0 → RETRACTED + flag for v1.8 followup". |
| Headline 78%→14% baseline doesn't reproduce — harness is stale | Low | Pre-reg stop condition: C2 late-phase must be within 4-24% (±10pp of 14%) or STOP. |
| Retraction sweep misses a claim location | Medium (codex P1) | Pre-eval `claim-inventory.md` artifact lists every grep hit. Retraction sweep must touch every listed location. |
| RETRACTED template soft-frames the result | Medium (was REJECT trigger) | Template stripped of "mechanism still useful as steering signal" framing. Says "claim withdrawn. Future eval may revisit." Period. |

## Constraints (from CLAUDE.md + project memory)

- **Real DB for tests.** Aggregator unit tests are pure math (no DB). Adapter contract tests load `interface.mjs` directly. No mocks.
- **Never `--no-verify`** on commits.
- **Atomic commit per task slice** + a separate commit for the prereg doc + a separate commit for the result doc.
- **TDD: failing test first** on Task 1 (contract validator) and Task 2 (aggregator math). Task 3 is an eval, not a code change — TDD doesn't apply.
- **Branch off master.**
- **Honest reporting (CRITICAL):** if the eval comes back null or worse-than-baseline, retract the claim. No soft framing. No "directional signal". The pre-registered template is what ships.
- **No public API change** in this release — adapter interface gains optional methods (additive). Multi-seed flags are CLI-only.
- **`run.mjs` and `aggregate.mjs` stay zero-dependency** (no npm imports beyond Node 22+ built-ins). The benchmark must run on a vanilla Node install.

# v1.7.6 — Discriminating Workload Variant for Goal-Stack Hypothesis Test

Source: https://github.com/kitfunso/hippo-memory/blob/master/docs/plans/2026-05-07-v1.7.6-discriminating-workload.md

# v1.7.6 — Discriminating Workload Variant for Goal-Stack Hypothesis Test

> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

> **Plan version:** v2 (post outside-voice review, 2026-05-07). v1 reviewed in parallel by `senior-code-reviewer` agent + `codex exec -m gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort=high`. Consolidated 22 revisions: 7 P0 (calibration N bumped 5→10 to clear `ciHalfWidth95` n<5 floor; **C2 sanity preflight inserted between C2 and C3 so SANITY_FAIL never collects goal-stack data**; calibration script schema fix to read `phases.late` not `seeds[0].phases.late`; hardened mechanical preflight script replaces `git log | grep`; explicit `simulate()` opts.budget diff; observable budget-delta test; soft-frame removed from NOT_SUPPORTED template), 10 P1 (Monte Carlo wording fix; calibration seed offset 100→10000 for non-collision; `computeVerdict` extracted + 5 fixture tests; starvation guard; within-band drift soft-warning; SANITY_FAIL causality fix; reproducibility logging; win32 smoke; "why budget" pre-reg paragraph; boundary tests), 5 P2 (time budget realism; drift soft-warning; README inventory grep; v1.7.7+ escalation pre-named; v1.7.5 forward-pointer in Task 4 not Task 7).

**Goal:** Re-run the v1.7.5 4-condition × 20-seed paired eval on a workload variant where C2 (hippo-base) lands inside the pre-registered sanity band [4%, 24%] late-phase trap-hit-rate, leaving headroom for the goal-stack mechanism to demonstrate (or fail to demonstrate) the −10pp lift hypothesis. Apply the v1.7.5 decision rule mechanically and update CHANGELOG / README / RESEARCH.md / TODOS.md per the verdict (DEMONSTRATED, NOT SUPPORTED, or SANITY_FAIL).

**Architecture:** Three logical pieces, all built on v1.7.5 infrastructure (do not rebuild). (1) **Budget plumbing** — `interface.mjs` `recall(query, budget?)`, `run.mjs` `--budget` flag, `hippo.mjs` honors it. The hardcoded `--budget 2000` in `hippo.mjs:84` is the single non-controllable variable blocking the calibration sweep. (2) **Calibration step** — new `benchmarks/sequential-learning/calibrate.mjs` runs C2 only across budget candidates {200, 400, 600, 800, 1000} with N=5 calibration seeds (range 100..104, distinct from hypothesis seeds 0..19), picks B* mechanically per a pre-registered rule (largest budget where C2 late ∈ [4%, 24%] AND lower-CI > 0%). (3) **Hypothesis run** — same v1.7.5 harness at `--budget B*` for 4 conditions × 20 seeds. Pre-registration document, claim inventory, and both report templates committed BEFORE the hypothesis run. New analyzer `analyze-v1.7.6.mjs` emits the verdict mechanically.

**Tech Stack:** Node 22.5+ (built-in `node:sqlite`, `node:crypto`), vitest, the v1.7.5 multi-seed harness (`run.mjs`, `aggregate.mjs`, `traps.mjs`), `pairedPermutationCI` (10k resamples), `hippo` CLI subprocess via `execSync`. No new dependencies.

## Pre-investigated facts (anchors — do not re-investigate)

**v1.7.5 shipped infrastructure (REUSE, do not rebuild):**
- `benchmarks/sequential-learning/adapters/interface.mjs` — `pushGoal/completeGoal` optional hooks present.
- `benchmarks/sequential-learning/adapters/hippo.mjs:84` — currently hardcodes `--budget 2000` in the `hippo recall` invocation. **This is the bug to fix in Task 1.**
- `benchmarks/sequential-learning/run.mjs` — `--seed`, `--n-seeds`, `--use-goal-stack`, `--eval-strict` flags present. **No `--budget` flag yet.** `simulate()` calls `adapter.recall(task.recallQuery)` without a budget arg.
- `benchmarks/sequential-learning/aggregate.mjs` — `mean`, `stdDev`, `ciHalfWidth95` (n<5 → 0), `aggregatePhases`, `pairedPermutationCI` (10k resamples). Reuse unchanged.
- `benchmarks/sequential-learning/traps.mjs::generateTasks(seed)` — seeded category-to-slot assignment within phase shape groups (EML, ELL, EM, ML). 25 trap encounters per seed.
- `benchmarks/sequential-learning/analyze-v1.7.5.mjs` — applies the v1.7.5 decision rule. Used as template for `analyze-v1.7.6.mjs`.
- Pre-registration convention: `docs/evals/YYYY-MM-DD-vX.Y.Z-goal-stack-eval-prereg.md` + `claim-inventory.md` + `result.md`.
- Seed derivation: `(Math.imul(0x9E3779B9, (1000 + i) >>> 0)) >>> 0` for i in 0..19. Calibration seeds: same formula with i in 100..104 (distinct hash space, avoids correlated mulberry32 streams between calibration and hypothesis runs).

**v1.7.5 result (the floor effect):**
- `docs/evals/2026-05-07-v1.7.5-goal-stack-eval-result.md` — C2 = 0.0%, C3 = 0.0%, ΔLate = 0pp. Sanity band [4%, 24%] FAIL. STOP. Floor diagnosis: `--budget 2000` × 50 tasks × 25 trap encounters fully suppresses late-phase traps regardless of goal-stack. Reducing `--budget` is the cleanest knob to put the workload back into the discriminating zone.

**Current hippo CLI surface (verified 2026-05-07):**
- `hippo recall "<query>" --json --budget <N>` — `--budget` parameter is honored end-to-end through `src/cli.ts::cmdRecall`. No CLI changes needed in `src/`.
- `hippo goal push <name>` — prints `g_<16hex>` id on stdout (already integrated by v1.7.5 hooks).
- `hippo goal complete <id> --outcome <0..1>` — already integrated.

**Public-surface status of the −10pp claim (post-v1.7.5):**
- The −10pp magnitude is currently **untested on a discriminating workload**. v1.7.5 explicitly framed itself as "mechanism shipped, hypothesis untested."
- Locations referencing the claim: `CHANGELOG.md` v1.7.5 entry (says STOPPED per sanity gate), `README.md` "What's new in v1.7.5" (same framing), `docs/plans/2026-04-29-b3-dlpfc-depth.md` (B3 stretch, header note already pointing to v1.7.5 result), `TODOS.md:144` (the v1.7.6+ followup line itself), `docs/evals/2026-05-07-v1.7.5-*` (frozen).
- v1.7.6 claim inventory (Task 4) re-walks these and adds any new locations.

**Time budget (extrapolated from v1.7.5 timing, post-review correction):**
- Calibration: 10 seeds × 5 budgets × Node startup (~200ms) × 25 trap encounters × ~150–300ms per `hippo recall` subprocess ≈ 10–15 min total.
- Hypothesis run: 4 conditions × 20 seeds. C0/C1 fast (~30s each). C2 ≈ 6–8 min. C3 ≈ 12–15 min (3 subprocesses per trap: pushGoal + recall + completeGoal). Total ≈ 20–25 min.
- C2 sanity preflight (post-review P0-2): ~6–8 min before C3 starts; if SANITY_FAIL, C3 never runs (saves 12–15 min).
- **Total wall time: 30–45 min realistic, 60 min worst case** if calibration drifts and re-sweep needed at finer granularity. Earlier estimate of "25 min" was optimistic — Node subprocess startup dominates at small budgets.

|------|------------|

Within-band overfit (e.g., calibration C2=18%, hypothesis C2=22%, both in band but Δ shifts) is NOT caught by the gate. ## Pre-registration commit ordering (CRITICAL — mechanically enforced, post-review P0-4)

The hypothesis eval **MUST NOT RUN** before the pre-reg doc and claim inventory are committed. Order:

1. Task 1 — budget plumbing (code + tests) → commit
2. Task 2 — calibration script (code + tests) → commit
3. Task 3 — run calibration → write `calibration-result.md` → commit
4. Task 4 — write pre-reg + claim inventory → commit (and append forward-pointer to v1.7.5 result doc per P2-5)
5. Task 5 — write `analyze-v1.7.6.mjs` + verdict tests → commit
6. Task 6 — preflight check (mechanical, see below) → run C2 → C2 sanity check → run C3 → analyze → write `result.md` → commit
7. Task 7 — apply consequences (CHANGELOG / README / RESEARCH.md / TODOS.md) → commit
8. Task 8 — `/self-review` → `/review` → `/ship-check` → `/publish-repo`

### Mechanical preflight script (Task 6 Step 1 — replaces the polite `git log | grep`)

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# (a) Required files exist on disk and are committed and reachable from HEAD.
for f in docs/evals/2026-05-07-v1.7.6-goal-stack-eval-prereg.md \
         docs/evals/2026-05-07-v1.7.6-claim-inventory.md \
         benchmarks/sequential-learning/analyze-v1.7.6.mjs \
         benchmarks/sequential-learning/results/v1.7.6-calibration/calibration-result.json; do
  test -f "$f" || { echo "STOP: $f missing on disk"; exit 1; }
  sha=$(git log -n1 --pretty=%H -- "$f" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [ -n "$sha" ] || { echo "STOP: $f has no commit"; exit 1; }
  git merge-base --is-ancestor "$sha" HEAD || { echo "STOP: $f commit unreachable from HEAD"; exit 1; }
done

# (b) Pre-reg pins the calibration B* value verbatim.
B_STAR=$(node -e "const j=JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('benchmarks/sequential-learning/results/v1.7.6-calibration/calibration-result.json'));console.log(j.bStar.budget)")
[ "$B_STAR" != "null" ] && [ -n "$B_STAR" ] || { echo "STOP: calibration B* = null; SANITY_FAIL escalation required"; exit 1; }
grep -qE "B\\\\* = ${B_STAR}\\b|--budget ${B_STAR}\\b|budget ${B_STAR}\\b" docs/evals/2026-05-07-v1.7.6-goal-stack-eval-prereg.md \
  || { echo "STOP: prereg does not pin B*=${B_STAR}"; exit 1; }

# (c) No eval result dirs already exist (would imply earlier silent run).
for d in v1.7.6-eval-C0-none v1.7.6-eval-C1-static v1.7.6-eval-C2-hippo-base v1.7.6-eval-C3-hippo-goalstack; do
  test ! -e "benchmarks/sequential-learning/results/$d" \
    || { echo "STOP: $d already exists; eval would not be a fresh run"; exit 1; }
done

# (d) Working tree clean.
[ -z "$(git status --porcelain)" ] || { echo "STOP: working tree dirty"; exit 1; }

echo "PREFLIGHT OK: B*=${B_STAR}, prereg pinned, no stale eval dirs, clean tree."
```

This script is the gate. If it fails, STOP — do not proceed under any speed directive. Pasting `--no-verify` style overrides on git commits remains forbidden per CLAUDE.md.

If at any step a sanity gate fires, STOP and document. Do not silently re-run with different parameters. Re-running requires a pre-reg amendment commit.

## Task 1: Plumb `--budget` through `run.mjs` → `adapter.recall(query, budget?)`

**Why first:** The hardcoded `--budget 2000` in `hippo.mjs:84` is the single non-controllable variable blocking calibration. This is a 30-line surgical change with backward-compat tests. Once shipped, calibration becomes a one-line invocation per budget candidate.

```typescript
// tests/sl-adapter-budget.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import hippoAdapter from '../benchmarks/sequential-learning/adapters/hippo.mjs';
import baselineAdapter from '../benchmarks/sequential-learning/adapters/baseline.mjs';
import staticAdapter from '../benchmarks/sequential-learning/adapters/static.mjs';

describe('sequential-learning adapter recall budget', () => {
  it('hippo adapter honors the budget arg with OBSERVABLE result-count delta at extreme budgets (post-review P0-6)', async () => {
    await hippoAdapter.init();
    try {
      // Seed with many memories so an extreme-low budget collapses the result set.
      for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
        await hippoAdapter.store(`lesson ${i}: do not commit broken code, item ${i}`, [
          'lesson',
          `lesson_${i}`,
        ]);
      }
      const wide = await hippoAdapter.recall('do not commit broken code', 2000);
      const tiny = await hippoAdapter.recall('do not commit broken code', 1);
      // Budget=1 must collapse the result set well below budget=2000. We assert
      // an OBSERVABLE delta (not just <=), so the test cannot pass if --budget
      // is silently ignored. If hippo's --budget enforcement is strict, tiny=0;
      // if lenient (returns at least 1 hit), it MUST be strictly fewer than wide.
      expect(wide.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3); // sanity: 30 memories, query matches
      expect(tiny.length).toBeLessThan(wide.length); // STRICT inequality, not <=
    } finally {
      await hippoAdapter.cleanup();
    }
  }, 60_000);

  it('hippo adapter defaults to 2000 when budget arg is omitted (backward compat)', async () => {
    await hippoAdapter.init();
    try {
      await hippoAdapter.store('compat lesson', ['compat']);
      // Single-arg signature must not throw.
      const results = await hippoAdapter.recall('compat lesson');
      expect(Array.isArray(results)).toBe(true);
    } finally {
      await hippoAdapter.cleanup();
    }
  }, 30_000);

  it('baseline adapter ignores the budget arg cleanly', async () => {
    await baselineAdapter.init();
    try {
      const r1 = await baselineAdapter.recall('anything', 100);
      const r2 = await baselineAdapter.recall('anything');
      // Baseline always returns []; budget arg must not throw.
      expect(r1).toEqual([]);
      expect(r2).toEqual([]);
    } finally {
      await baselineAdapter.cleanup();
    }
  });

  it('static adapter ignores the budget arg cleanly', async () => {
    await staticAdapter.init();
    try {
      const r1 = await staticAdapter.recall('overwrite production', 100);
      const r2 = await staticAdapter.recall('overwrite production');
      // Static returns the full pre-loaded lesson set; budget arg must not throw.
      expect(Array.isArray(r1)).toBe(true);
      expect(Array.isArray(r2)).toBe(true);
    } finally {
      await staticAdapter.cleanup();
    }
  });
});

## Task 2: Calibration script

**Why a separate script (not a flag on `run.mjs`):** Calibration runs C2 only across multiple budgets and emits a different result shape (per-budget table, not per-condition). Mixing into `run.mjs` would risk polluting the hypothesis-run code path with a calibration-only branch. A separate `calibrate.mjs` keeps the hypothesis runner's contract immutable.

**Files:**
- Create: `benchmarks/sequential-learning/calibrate.mjs`
- Test: `tests/sl-calibrate.test.ts` (NEW — unit-tests on the budget-selection rule, NOT the full subprocess sweep)

**Step 1: Write the failing test**

```typescript
// tests/sl-calibrate.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { selectBStar } from '../benchmarks/sequential-learning/calibrate.mjs';

import { mulberry32 } from '../benchmarks/sequential-learning/aggregate.mjs';

describe('v1.7.6 calibration B* selection', () => {
  it('picks the LARGEST budget where C2 late mean ∈ [0.04, 0.24] AND lower-CI > 0', () => {
    const candidates = [
      { budget: 200, lateMean: 0.30, lateCI: 0.05 }, // mean too high
      { budget: 400, lateMean: 0.20, lateCI: 0.05 }, // in band, lower-CI=0.15 > 0 ✓
      { budget: 600, lateMean: 0.10, lateCI: 0.05 }, // in band, lower-CI=0.05 > 0 ✓
      { budget: 800, lateMean: 0.05, lateCI: 0.06 }, // in band, lower-CI=-0.01 < 0 ✗
      { budget: 1000, lateMean: 0.02, lateCI: 0.01 }, // too low ✗
    ];
    const bStar = selectBStar(candidates);
    expect(bStar.budget).toBe(600); // largest passing
    expect(bStar.reason).toMatch(/in band/i);
  });

  it('returns null when no candidate qualifies', () => {
    const candidates = [
      { budget: 200, lateMean: 0.40, lateCI: 0.05 },
      { budget: 400, lateMean: 0.30, lateCI: 0.05 },
      { budget: 800, lateMean: 0.02, lateCI: 0.01 },
    ];
    const bStar = selectBStar(candidates);
    expect(bStar.budget).toBeNull();
    expect(bStar.reason).toMatch(/no candidate/i);
  });

  it('handles empty input', () => {
    expect(selectBStar([]).budget).toBeNull();
  });

  it('rejects candidate with mean exactly at boundary lower-CI=0', () => {
    // mean=0.04 with CI=0.04 → lower-CI = 0.0, NOT > 0, so reject.
    const candidates = [
      { budget: 400, lateMean: 0.04, lateCI: 0.04 },
    ];
    expect(selectBStar(candidates).budget).toBeNull();
  });

  // Post-review P1-10 — boundary positive case
  it('accepts candidate at lower band boundary with positive lower-CI', () => {
    // mean=0.04 with CI=0.039 → lower-CI = 0.001 > 0, accept.
    const candidates = [
      { budget: 400, lateMean: 0.04, lateCI: 0.039 },
    ];
    expect(selectBStar(candidates).budget).toBe(400);
  });

  // Post-review P1-10 — boundary negative case (mean below band)
  it('rejects candidate just below band even with zero CI', () => {
    // mean=0.0399 < BAND_LOW=0.04 → reject regardless of CI.
    const candidates = [
      { budget: 400, lateMean: 0.0399, lateCI: 0.0 },
    ];
    expect(selectBStar(candidates).budget).toBeNull();
  });

  // Post-review P1-1 — calibration vs hypothesis seed-stream non-collision
  it('calibration and hypothesis mulberry32 streams are pairwise distinct in first 50 draws', () => {
    // Hypothesis seeds: 1000 + i for i in 0..19
    const hypoSeeds = Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, i) =>
      (Math.imul(0x9E3779B9, (1000 + i) >>> 0)) >>> 0,
    );
    // Calibration seeds (post-review P1-1 — bumped offset 100 → 10000): 1000 + 10000 + i for i in 0..9
    const calibSeeds = Array.from({ length: 10 }, (_, i) =>
      (Math.imul(0x9E3779B9, (1000 + 10000 + i) >>> 0)) >>> 0,
    );
    const allSeeds = [...hypoSeeds, ...calibSeeds];
    const draws = allSeeds.map((s) => {
      const rng = mulberry32(s);
      return Array.from({ length: 50 }, () => rng());
    });
    // Pairwise: no two seed streams produce identical first 50 draws.
    for (let i = 0; i < draws.length; i++) {
      for (let j = i + 1; j < draws.length; j++) {
        const same = draws[i].every((v, k) => v === draws[j][k]);
        expect(same).toBe(false);
      }
    }
  });
});
```

**Step 3: Write `calibrate.mjs`**

Create `benchmarks/sequential-learning/calibrate.mjs`:

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * v1.7.6 -- Calibration sweep for the discriminating-workload variant.
 *
 * Runs C2 (hippo-base, no goal-stack) at a fixed list of budget candidates
 * with N=10 calibration seeds (post-review P0-1 -- ciHalfWidth95 returns 0
 * for n<5; n=10 gives a usable t-band). Calibration seeds: 1000+10000+i
 * for i in 0..9 (post-review P1-1 -- offset bumped from 100 to 10000 for
 * larger input distance vs hypothesis seeds 1000+i for i in 0..19).
 *
 * Picks B* mechanically per the pre-registered selection rule:
 *   B* = LARGEST budget where (mean late ∈ [0.04, 0.24]) AND (lower-CI > 0)
 *        AND mean(len(results)) >= 1 across calibration seeds (P1-4
 *        starvation guard).
 *
 * Outputs:
 *   - stdout: markdown table + B* announcement
 *   - <output>/calibration-result.json: structured per-budget rows
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node benchmarks/sequential-learning/calibrate.mjs \
 *     --budgets 200,400,600,800,1000 \
 *     --n-seeds 10 \
 *     --output benchmarks/sequential-learning/results/v1.7.6-calibration/
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, dirname } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { mean, ciHalfWidth95 } from './aggregate.mjs';

const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// B* selection rule (pre-registered in
// docs/evals/2026-05-07-v1.7.6-goal-stack-eval-prereg.md).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const BAND_LOW = 0.04;
const BAND_HIGH = 0.24;

/**
 * @param {Array<{budget:number, lateMean:number, lateCI:number, starved?:boolean}>} candidates
 * @returns {{budget:number|null, reason:string}}
 *
 * Post-review P1-4 -- starvation guard: if a candidate is flagged `starved`
 * (mean recall surface < 1 across calibration seeds), exclude before applying
 * the band rule.
 */
export function selectBStar(candidates) {
  if (!candidates || candidates.length === 0) {
    return { budget: null, reason: 'No candidates supplied.' };
  }
  // Sort descending by budget; pick the first that qualifies.
  const sorted = [...candidates].sort((a, b) => b.budget - a.budget);
  for (const c of sorted) {
    if (c.starved === true) continue; // P1-4 starvation exclusion
    const lowerCI = c.lateMean - c.lateCI;
    if (
      c.lateMean >= BAND_LOW &&
      c.lateMean <= BAND_HIGH &&
      lowerCI > 0
    ) {
      return {
        budget: c.budget,
        reason: `largest budget in band [${BAND_LOW}, ${BAND_HIGH}] with lower-CI ${lowerCI.toFixed(4)} > 0 (not starved)`,
      };
    }
  }
  return {
    budget: null,
    reason: `No candidate satisfies (mean ∈ [${BAND_LOW}, ${BAND_HIGH}]) AND (lower-CI > 0) AND (not starved).`,
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// CLI driver (no-op when imported from tests)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function parseArgs() {
  const args = process.argv.slice(2);
  const opts = {
    budgets: [200, 400, 600, 800, 1000],
    nSeeds: 10, // post-review P0-1 -- bumped from 5 to 10 for usable CI.
    output: join(__dirname, 'results', 'v1.7.6-calibration'),
  };
  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
    if (args[i] === '--budgets' && args[i + 1]) {
      opts.budgets = args[++i].split(',').map((s) => parseInt(s, 10));
    } else if (args[i] === '--n-seeds' && args[i + 1]) {
      opts.nSeeds = parseInt(args[++i], 10);
    } else if (args[i] === '--output' && args[i + 1]) {
      opts.output = args[++i];
    }
  }
  return opts;
}

function deriveCalibrationSeeds(n) {
  // Post-review P1-1 -- offset bumped from 100 to 10000 for larger input
  // distance vs hypothesis seeds (1000+i for i in 0..19). Pairwise non-collision
  // verified by tests/sl-calibrate.test.ts.
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) =>
    (Math.imul(0x9E3779B9, (1000 + 10000 + i) >>> 0)) >>> 0,
  );
}

function runOneBudget(budget, seeds, outputBase) {
  const outDir = join(outputBase, `budget-${budget}`);
  if (!existsSync(outDir)) mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });

  // Post-review P0-3 -- run.mjs sets `seedRuns: null` for single-seed runs
  // (run.mjs:548 -- `seedList.length > 1 ? seedRuns : null`). The single-seed
  // late rate lives at j.conditions[condName].phases.late, NOT at
  // j.conditions[condName].seeds[0].phases.late. Reading the wrong path
  // crashes silently (`Cannot read properties of null`).
  //
  // We invoke run.mjs once per calibration seed via --seed <hash>.
  const seedRates = [];
  const seedResultCounts = []; // post-review P1-4 -- starvation guard.
  for (const seed of seeds) {
    const seedDir = join(outDir, `seed-${seed}`);
    if (!existsSync(seedDir)) mkdirSync(seedDir, { recursive: true });
    execSync(
      `node "${join(__dirname, 'run.mjs')}" --adapter hippo --seed ${seed} --budget ${budget} --output "${seedDir}"`,
      { stdio: 'inherit' },
    );
    // Read the resulting JSON and extract late-phase rate for this single seed.
    const files = readdirSync(seedDir).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.json'));
    if (files.length === 0) throw new Error(`No JSON output in ${seedDir}`);
    files.sort();
    const j = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(seedDir, files[files.length - 1]), 'utf-8'));
    const condName = Object.keys(j.conditions)[0];
    // Single-seed path -- read directly from `phases.late`.
    const lateRate = j.conditions[condName].phases.late;
    if (typeof lateRate !== 'number') {
      throw new Error(
        `runOneBudget: phases.late not numeric for ${seedDir} (got ${typeof lateRate}). ` +
        `Schema may have changed; verify run.mjs:539-550 output shape.`,
      );
    }
    seedRates.push(lateRate);

    // Starvation guard -- count avg results returned per trap encounter.
    // results[].memoryRecalled is true iff recall returned a matching memory;
    // we approximate avg recall surface from `results.length` of trap tasks
    // (which is fixed at ~25) vs how many had memoryRecalled. Real per-trap
    // result-count is not surfaced in run.mjs JSON; use a simpler heuristic:
    // if zero traps had memoryRecalled across the whole seed, the budget
    // is starving the BM25 ranker.
    const trapResults = (j.conditions[condName].results ?? []).filter(
      (r) => r.trapCategory !== null,
    );
    const recalledCount = trapResults.filter((r) => r.memoryRecalled).length;
    seedResultCounts.push(recalledCount);
  }
  const starvationFlag =
    seedResultCounts.length > 0 &&
    seedResultCounts.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / seedResultCounts.length < 1;
  return {
    budget,
    seedRates,
    seedResultCounts,
    starved: starvationFlag,
    lateMean: mean(seedRates),
    lateCI: ciHalfWidth95(seedRates),
  };
}

async function main() {
  const opts = parseArgs();
  if (!existsSync(opts.output)) mkdirSync(opts.output, { recursive: true });

  const seeds = deriveCalibrationSeeds(opts.nSeeds);
  console.log(`Calibration seeds (n=${opts.nSeeds}): ${seeds.join(', ')}`);
  console.log(`Budget candidates: ${opts.budgets.join(', ')}`);
  console.log('');

  const rows = [];
  for (const budget of opts.budgets) {
    console.log(`--- budget=${budget} ---`);
    const row = runOneBudget(budget, seeds, opts.output);
    rows.push(row);
    console.log(
      `  late mean=${(row.lateMean * 100).toFixed(2)}% ±${(row.lateCI * 100).toFixed(2)}pp ` +
      `(seeds: ${row.seedRates.map((r) => (r * 100).toFixed(1) + '%').join(', ')})`,
    );
  }

  const bStar = selectBStar(rows);
  console.log('');
  console.log('# Calibration Summary');
  console.log('| Budget | Late mean | ±95% CI | Lower-CI | In band? |');
  console.log('|--------|-----------|---------|----------|----------|');
  for (const r of rows) {
    const lowerCI = r.lateMean - r.lateCI;
    const inBand =
      r.lateMean >= BAND_LOW && r.lateMean <= BAND_HIGH && lowerCI > 0
        ? 'YES'
        : 'no';
    console.log(
      `| ${r.budget} | ${(r.lateMean * 100).toFixed(2)}% | ±${(r.lateCI * 100).toFixed(2)}pp | ${(lowerCI * 100).toFixed(2)}pp | ${inBand} |`,
    );
  }
  console.log('');
  console.log(`B* = ${bStar.budget ?? 'NONE'} (${bStar.reason})`);

  // Write structured JSON
  writeFileSync(
    join(opts.output, 'calibration-result.json'),
    JSON.stringify({ rows, bStar, seeds, candidates: opts.budgets }, null, 2),
  );
}

// Only run main() when invoked as a script. When imported (by tests), skip.
const invokedAsScript =
  process.argv[1] && fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === process.argv[1];
if (invokedAsScript) {
  main().catch((err) => {
    console.error(err);
    process.exit(1);
  });
}
```

```markdown
# v1.7.6 Calibration — Result

**Run:** 2026-05-07
**Pre-registered selection rule:** B* = LARGEST budget where (mean late ∈ [4%, 24%]) AND (lower-CI > 0) AND (not starved).
**Calibration seeds (n=10, post-review P0-1):** {paste from stdout}, hash-derived from `1000 + 10000 + i` for i in 0..9 (post-review P1-1 — offset bumped from 100 to 10000 for non-collision with hypothesis seeds `1000 + i` for i in 0..19).
**Candidates:** 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000.

## Reproducibility anchors

- `hippo --version` = {paste output}
- `which hippo` = {paste output}
- `git rev-parse HEAD` = {paste sha}
- `node --version` = {paste output}
- Wall time = {minutes:seconds}

## Per-budget late-phase trap rate (C2 only)

| Budget | Late mean | ±95% CI | Lower-CI | Avg recall surface | Starved? | In band? |

**Step 1: Write `2026-05-07-v1.7.6-goal-stack-eval-prereg.md`**

```markdown
# v1.7.6 Goal-Stack Eval — Pre-Registration

**Pre-registered:** 2026-05-07, BEFORE running the hypothesis eval.
**Author:** Keith So
**Mechanism under test:** B3 dlPFC goal-stack boost (`applyGoalStackBoost`), shipped v1.7.4.
**Workload variant:** discriminating budget B* = {VALUE_FROM_TASK_3}, picked by mechanical selection rule documented in `docs/evals/2026-05-07-v1.7.6-calibration-result.md` and `benchmarks/sequential-learning/calibrate.mjs::selectBStar`.
**Public-surface status of the claim:** the −10pp hypothesis was not testable in v1.7.5 due to floor effect (C2 = 0.0% late). v1.7.6 re-tests on the calibrated workload; result is "supported / not supported", published with measured numbers + CIs either way.

## Hypothesis

H₁: Activating the dlPFC goal-stack boost on top of base hippo reduces late-phase trap-hit-rate by ≥10 percentage points on the v1.7.6 discriminating workload (`--budget B*`), with 95% CI lower bound > 0pp.

H₀: Activation produces no detectable improvement (95% CI for Δ overlaps 0).

## Protocol

- Benchmark: `benchmarks/sequential-learning` (v1.7.5 multi-seed harness, unchanged).
- **Workload knob (NEW for v1.7.6):** `--budget {B*}` (selected by Task 3 calibration).
- **Conditions (4):** C0 none, C1 static, C2 hippo-base (`--use-goal-stack` OFF), C3 hippo+goalstack (`--use-goal-stack` ON).
- **Hypothesis seeds: 20.** Hash-derived in `run.mjs` (`Math.imul(0x9E3779B9, 1000+i) >>> 0` for i in 0..19). Distinct from calibration seeds (1000+100+i for i in 0..4).
- **Eval mode:** `--eval-strict`.
- **Primary metric:** late-phase trap-hit-rate (existing `hitRateByPhase`, last 8 of 25 trap encounters).
- **Top-5 cap interaction:** unchanged from v1.7.5.

## Statistical method (PRE-LOCKED, unchanged from v1.7.5 — wording corrected post-review P1-2)

- Estimand: mean late-phase Δ in pp = `mean_late(C2) − mean_late(C3)` over 20 paired seeds.
- CI: 10,000 Monte Carlo resamples of paired sign-flip permutation (`pairedPermutationCI` in `aggregate.mjs`). For n=20, full enumeration would be 2^20 ≈ 1M sign-flip combinations; 10k Monte Carlo draws are sufficient for stable percentile bounds. NOT t-test — phase rates are bounded discrete.
- For ties heavy at 0% (last-8 of bounded discrete trap encounters), Monte Carlo permutation may produce wide CI; result doc reports tie distribution alongside the CI for transparency.

## Decision rule (mechanical)

Compute Δ and 95% permutation CI on Δ.

- **Δ ≥ 0.10 AND lower-CI > 0** → **HYPOTHESIS SUPPORTED.** Ship "SUPPORTED" template.
- **Δ < 0.10 OR CI overlaps 0** → **HYPOTHESIS NOT SUPPORTED.** Ship "NOT SUPPORTED" template citing measured Δ and CI.
- **Δ < 0 with upper-CI < 0** = goal-stack measurably HARMS performance. Flag for v1.8 design review.

## Stop conditions (mid-run)

- **Sanity gate** (re-fires at hypothesis-run scale): if C2 late mean at N=20 is outside [0.04, 0.24], STOP. Write `result.md` with SANITY_FAIL verdict; document drift; do NOT silently re-calibrate. Re-calibration requires a pre-reg amendment commit.
- **Hook failure gate:** if `C3.hookFailures.push > 0` OR `.complete > 0`, STOP. Run contaminated.
- **Seed crash policy:** drop the seed across ALL conditions (paired); replacement seed indexed 1020+. No cherry-picking.
- **Outlier policy:** any single seed >3σ from the rest in either condition → investigate and document.

## Calibration → hypothesis link

The B* picked by Task 3 calibration is locked into this pre-reg's `--budget` parameter. Calibration uses seed input range `1000 + 10000 + i` for i in 0..9 (10 seeds, post-review P0-1 + P1-1); hypothesis uses `1000 + i` for i in 0..19 (20 seeds). Hash-derived from `0x9E3779B9` so the two ranges are deterministic, reproducible, and non-overlapping (verified pairwise distinct by unit test).

The sanity gate re-fires AT THE C2 STAGE of the hypothesis run (post-review P0-2). If drift moves C2 out of band, STOP — C3 is NOT collected. This avoids leaking goal-stack directional data on a "stopped" eval.

**Within-band overfit caveat (post-review P1-5):** the sanity gate detects only out-of-band drift. If calibration C2 = 18% and hypothesis C2 = 22% (both in band but drift > 5pp), the result doc must report both side-by-side and flag the drift as a soft warning even on SUPPORTED.

## Why budget reduction, not the other 4 workload variants (post-review P1-9)

v1.7.5 result lists 5 candidate workload variants. This pre-reg picks budget reduction first because:

1. **Single CLI knob.** No new code surface; `--budget` already exists end-to-end (Task 1 lifts the hardcoded 2000).
2. **Monotone effect.** Smaller budget = harder retrieval. No semantic change to traps or metric.
3. **No C3 exposure during workload selection.** Calibration runs C2 only; goal-stack is never invoked at the calibration stage.
4. **Doesn't require new lesson authoring.** Adversarial categories would need new trap text; that's v1.8 scope.
5. **Doesn't redefine the metric.** Restricting the late-phase window changes what "late" means; that's v1.7.7 fallback.

Pre-committed escalation order (post-review P2-4):
- If v1.7.6 SANITY_FAILs → v1.7.7 will be `--restrict-late-to last-4` (deterministic, single-line workload tweak).
- If v1.7.7 also fails → v1.8 explores adversarial trap categories (requires new lesson authoring + harness changes).
- LongMemEval R@5 corpus is a separate eval line, not a substitute.

**Step 3: Refactor verdict computation into a pure exported function**

Extract from the analyzer body into the top of the module:

```javascript
/**
 * Pure verdict computation. No I/O. Testable in isolation.
 * @param {{c2Late:number, c3Late:number, delta:number, ciLow:number, ciHigh:number,
 *          hookFailures:{push:number, complete:number}|null,
 *          sanityPass:boolean}} input
 * @returns {'SUPPORTED' | 'NOT_SUPPORTED' | 'SANITY_FAIL' | 'HOOK_FAIL'}
 */
export function computeVerdict({ c2Late, c3Late, delta, ciLow, ciHigh, hookFailures, sanityPass }) {
  if (!sanityPass) return 'SANITY_FAIL';
  if ((hookFailures?.push ?? 0) > 0 || (hookFailures?.complete ?? 0) > 0) return 'HOOK_FAIL';
  if (delta >= 0.10 && ciLow > 0) return 'SUPPORTED';
  return 'NOT_SUPPORTED';
}
```

The analyzer's bottom-of-file `verdict` derivation calls `computeVerdict({...})` instead of recomputing inline.

**Step 4: Write the verdict-emission test**

```typescript
// tests/sl-analyze-v1.7.6.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { computeVerdict } from '../benchmarks/sequential-learning/analyze-v1.7.6.mjs';

describe('v1.7.6 computeVerdict', () => {
  it('returns SUPPORTED when delta >= 0.10 AND ciLow > 0 AND sanity passes', () => {
    expect(computeVerdict({
      c2Late: 0.18, c3Late: 0.05, delta: 0.13,
      ciLow: 0.04, ciHigh: 0.22,
      hookFailures: { push: 0, complete: 0 }, sanityPass: true,
    })).toBe('SUPPORTED');
  });

  it('returns NOT_SUPPORTED when delta < 0.10', () => {
    expect(computeVerdict({
      c2Late: 0.18, c3Late: 0.13, delta: 0.05,
      ciLow: 0.01, ciHigh: 0.09,
      hookFailures: { push: 0, complete: 0 }, sanityPass: true,
    })).toBe('NOT_SUPPORTED');
  });

  it('returns NOT_SUPPORTED when ciLow <= 0 even if delta >= 0.10', () => {
    expect(computeVerdict({
      c2Late: 0.18, c3Late: 0.05, delta: 0.13,
      ciLow: -0.02, ciHigh: 0.28,
      hookFailures: { push: 0, complete: 0 }, sanityPass: true,
    })).toBe('NOT_SUPPORTED');
  });

  it('returns SANITY_FAIL when sanityPass is false (overrides everything)', () => {
    expect(computeVerdict({
      c2Late: 0.0, c3Late: 0.0, delta: 0.0,
      ciLow: 0.0, ciHigh: 0.0,
      hookFailures: { push: 0, complete: 0 }, sanityPass: false,
    })).toBe('SANITY_FAIL');
  });

  it('returns HOOK_FAIL when sanity passes but hook failures > 0', () => {
    expect(computeVerdict({
      c2Late: 0.18, c3Late: 0.05, delta: 0.13,
      ciLow: 0.04, ciHigh: 0.22,
      hookFailures: { push: 1, complete: 0 }, sanityPass: true,
    })).toBe('HOOK_FAIL');
  });
});
```

**Step 4.5: C2 SANITY PREFLIGHT (post-review P0-2, CRITICAL — must run BEFORE C3)**

Mechanically verify C2 late mean lands inside [0.04, 0.24] AND lower-CI > 0 BEFORE collecting any C3 data. If sanity fails, C3 is NOT collected — goal-stack data will not be produced, ensuring a "stopped" eval cannot leak directional information.

```bash
node -e "
  const fs = require('node:fs');
  const path = require('node:path');
  const { mean, ciHalfWidth95 } = require('./benchmarks/sequential-learning/aggregate.mjs');
  const dir = 'benchmarks/sequential-learning/results/v1.7.6-eval-C2-hippo-base';
  const files = fs.readdirSync(dir).filter(f => f.endsWith('.json')).sort();
  const j = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, files[files.length - 1]), 'utf-8'));
  const condName = Object.keys(j.conditions)[0];
  const lateRates = j.conditions[condName].seedRuns.map(r => r.phases.late);
  const m = mean(lateRates);
  const ci = ciHalfWidth95(lateRates);
  const lowerCI = m - ci;
  const inBand = m >= 0.04 && m <= 0.24 && lowerCI > 0;
  console.log('C2 late: mean=' + (m*100).toFixed(2) + '%, CI=±' + (ci*100).toFixed(2) + 'pp, lower-CI=' + (lowerCI*100).toFixed(2) + 'pp');
  console.log('Sanity gate: ' + (inBand ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL') + ' (band [4%, 24%], lower-CI > 0)');
  if (!inBand) {
    console.error('STOP: C2 sanity FAIL. C3 will NOT be collected. Apply Task 7 SANITY_FAIL branch.');
    process.exit(1);
  }
" || { echo "C2 sanity FAILED — STOP. Skip Step 5 (C3). Apply SANITY_FAIL branch in Task 7."; exit 1; }
```

If sanity FAILS:
- Skip Step 5 entirely (do NOT collect C3).
- Skip Step 6 (analyzer needs all 4 conditions).
- Jump to Step 8 with verdict pre-determined as `SANITY_FAIL`.
- The result doc must explicitly state "C3 not collected; goal-stack data not produced this run."
- Apply Task 7 Branch 7-C (SANITY_FAIL).

If sanity PASSES → continue to Step 5.

# v1.7.7 — Restricted Late-Phase Window for Goal-Stack Hypothesis Test

Source: https://github.com/kitfunso/hippo-memory/blob/master/docs/plans/2026-05-09-v1.7.7-restricted-late-window.md

# v1.7.7 — Restricted Late-Phase Window for Goal-Stack Hypothesis Test

> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

> **Plan version:** v2 (post outside-voice review, 2026-05-09). v1 reviewed in parallel by `senior-code-reviewer` agent + `codex exec -m gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort=high`. Consolidated 16 revisions: **4 P0** (`run.mjs` made import-safe BEFORE exports — codex caught that `main()` ran unconditionally and would spawn hippo subprocesses on every test import; preflight regex tightened from `\b` to non-digit boundary; C2 sanity band recalibrated for the N=4 lattice; goalposts hard-stop + cumulative-evidence retraction clause), **8 P1** (cross-version comparability lock; tie-degeneracy guard + paired-diff histogram; exact-enumeration sensitivity check at near-threshold; cliff humility; preflight runs analyzer + slice-math tests; inline starvation warning at C2 sanity; reproducibility blob refs; v1.8 pre-commit constraints), **4 P2** (test coverage gaps; name-shadow comment; shell-quirk warning; time-budget realism).

**Goal:** Test whether the goal-stack mechanism produces a ≥10pp drop in late-phase trap-hit-rate when the late-phase metric is narrowed from "last third (7 traps)" to "last 4 trap encounters". v1.7.6 confirmed budget reduction does not discriminate; this plan acts on the pre-committed v1.7.7 escalation. Verdict is DEMONSTRATED, NOT_SUPPORTED, or SANITY_FAIL — published with measured numbers + CIs in every case.

**Architecture:** Three logical pieces, all built on v1.7.5/v1.7.6 infrastructure (do not rebuild). (1) **Workload knob** — `--restrict-late-to <int>` flag on `run.mjs`. When set, late slice = last N trap encounters; early/mid re-split to "first ceil((total-N)/2)" / "remainder" so the three slices stay disjoint and total to all trap tasks. Default `null` preserves current chronological-third behavior. `buildOutput()` records the value in result JSON for audit. (2) **C2 sanity preflight** — same C2-before-C3 design from v1.7.6 P0-2: run C2 only at `--budget 2000 --restrict-late-to 4 --n-seeds 20 --eval-strict`, mechanically check C2 late mean ∈ [0.04, 0.24] AND lower-CI > 0; on FAIL, STOP, do NOT collect C3, retarget to v1.8 adversarial categories. (3) **Hypothesis run + decision** — only if C2 sanity passes. Run C0, C1, C3 at the same workload; analyzer emits verdict (SUPPORTED / NOT_SUPPORTED / SANITY_FAIL / HOOK_FAIL) per pre-registered rule. All three verdict templates committed BEFORE the run.

**Tech Stack:** Node 22.5+ (built-in `node:sqlite`), vitest, the v1.7.5 multi-seed harness (`run.mjs`, `aggregate.mjs`, `traps.mjs`), `pairedPermutationCI` (10k Monte Carlo resamples), `hippo` CLI subprocess via `execSync`. No new dependencies. The starvation-guard re-enable is **deferred to a later release** (see "Scope decisions" below) to keep the v1.7.7 narrative tight on the metric switch.

---

## Pre-investigated facts (anchors — do not re-investigate)

**v1.7.5 / v1.7.6 shipped infrastructure (REUSE, do not rebuild):**
- `--budget` flag end-to-end through `run.mjs` → `simulate()` → `adapter.recall(query, budget)`. Default 2000. **For v1.7.7 budget stays at default — budget is NOT the knob.**
- `benchmarks/sequential-learning/run.mjs::simulate()` accepts `opts.useGoalStack`, `opts.evalStrict`, `opts.budget`. v1.7.7 adds `opts.restrictLateTo`.
- `benchmarks/sequential-learning/run.mjs::hitRateByPhase(results)` (lines 314–329). With 25 trap tasks: third = ceil(25/3) = 9. early=slice(0,9), mid=slice(9,18), late=slice(18) — i.e. **late = last 7 trap encounters**, not 8. The v1.7.5 prereg's "late = last 8" was documentation drift; v1.7.7 corrects to actual `last 7` when restrictLateTo is null.
- `benchmarks/sequential-learning/aggregate.mjs` — `mean`, `stdDev`, `ciHalfWidth95` (returns 0 for n<5; n=20 uses t=2.093), `aggregatePhases`, `pairedPermutationCI` (10k Monte Carlo). Reuse unchanged.
- `benchmarks/sequential-learning/traps.mjs::generateTasks(seed)` — seeded category-to-slot variance. Always produces 25 trap encounters per 50-task seed.
- `benchmarks/sequential-learning/analyze-v1.7.5.mjs` — analyzer template. Single-seed schema confirmed (no per-task `results` in JSON; phase data lives at `j.conditions[cn].phases.{early,mid,late}` and per-seed at `j.conditions[cn].seeds[i].phases.late`). v1.7.6 plan post-review extracted `computeVerdict` into a pure function — adopt same pattern for v1.7.7.
- Hypothesis seeds: `Math.imul(0x9E3779B9, (1000 + i) >>> 0) >>> 0` for i in 0..19. **Reused identically — same paired structure as v1.7.5/v1.7.6.**
- v1.7.6 plan post-review (commit `c670ac9`): hardened mechanical preflight script (P0-4), C2-before-C3 sanity (P0-2), reproducibility-anchor capture (P1-7), no-soft-frame NOT_SUPPORTED template (P0-7), Monte Carlo wording (P1-2). **Adopt verbatim where applicable.**

**v1.7.6 result (the calibration finding to forward-point from):**
- `docs/evals/2026-05-09-v1.7.6-calibration-result.md` — B*=NULL across 5 budgets × 10 seeds; lateMean=0% on every run with default chronological-third late slice. "Floor effect is structural to the 50-task workload, not budget-tunable."
- v1.7.6 CHANGELOG and README pre-committed: "v1.7.7 will sweep `--restrict-late-to last-4`."
- v1.7.6 plan TODOS line: "Re-enable starvation guard in `calibrate.mjs` with correct schema → v1.7.7+." (See "Scope decisions" — deferred.)

**Public-surface status of the −10pp claim (post-v1.7.6, unchanged):**
- The −10pp magnitude is **untested on a discriminating workload**. v1.7.5 saturated, v1.7.6 confirmed budget reduction doesn't bite.
- Locations to walk in claim inventory: `CHANGELOG.md` v1.7.5 + v1.7.6 entries, `README.md` "What's new" sections, `docs/plans/2026-04-29-b3-dlpfc-depth.md` (B3 stretch), `TODOS.md` (the v1.7.7 line itself plus the v1.7.7+ starvation-guard line), `docs/evals/2026-05-07-v1.7.5-goal-stack-eval-result.md` (forward-pointer block), `docs/evals/2026-05-09-v1.7.6-calibration-result.md` (forward-pointer block), `RESEARCH.md` (verify).

**Slice math (Option A — locked):**
- Total trap tasks per seed = 25 (deterministic from `traps.mjs`).
- When `restrictLateTo` is `null` (default): late = last 7 (`slice(18)`), early = first 9 (`slice(0,9)`), mid = middle 9 (`slice(9,18)`). Backward-compatible.
- When `restrictLateTo = N` with `N ∈ [1, 25]`: late = last N (`slice(25-N)`), early = first `ceil((25-N)/2)`, mid = remainder.
  - N=4 (the v1.7.7 hypothesis workload): early = first 11 (positions 1-11), mid = 10 (positions 12-21), late = 4 (positions 22-25). Total 25 ✓.
  - N=8 (close to v1.7.5 default): early = ceil(17/2)=9, mid = 8, late = 8. Slightly different from chronological-third (which gives early=9, mid=9, late=7), but disjoint and exhaustive.
- Edge cases: N=0 → late slice empty, return 0; N>25 → late = all traps (early=mid=empty); N<0 → reject in parseArgs with parseInt-NaN-style error.

**Time budget (extrapolated from v1.7.6, post-review P2-4 raised):**
- Task 1 (flag plumbing + tests + import-safety wrap): ~40 min code work.
- Task 2 (pre-reg + claim inventory + v1.8 pre-commit constraints): ~40 min doc work.
- Task 3 (analyzer + verdict tests + tie-degeneracy guard): ~30 min code work.
- Task 4 (C2 preflight + reproducibility blob refs): ~6-8 min subprocess + ~5 min doc work.
- Task 5 (hypothesis run if C2 passes): ~25-35 min subprocess. Realistic per-condition: C0 ~30s; C1 ~30s; C2 ~6-8 min (~20s/seed × 20 seeds at default budget 2000); C3 ~20-30 min (3 hippo subprocess calls per trap-encounter — `pushGoal` + `recall` + `completeGoal` × 25 trap encounters × 20 seeds).
- Task 6 (consequences): ~30 min doc work.
- Task 7 (ship): ~15 min.
- **Total wall time: 2-3 hours; subprocess work: ~35-50 min if C2 passes, ~8-10 min if C2 fails.**

## Scope decisions (locked before any code touches)

**1. Slice math: Option A (locked).** Late = last N. Early/mid re-split to "first ceil((total-N)/2)" / "remainder". Disjoint, exhaustive, deterministic. Backward-compatible when `restrictLateTo` is null.

**2. Workload knob: window restriction only.** Budget stays at default 2000 (v1.7.6 confirmed budget isn't the knob). `--use-goal-stack` toggles between C2 and C3. No new workload axes introduced.

**3. Starvation-guard re-enable: DEFERRED.** v1.7.6 plan named this as a "v1.7.7+" task. v1.7.7 ships ONE workload knob change to keep the eval narrative tight; folding in a new schema change to `buildOutput()` would muddy the C2 preflight investigation if it FAILed. Tracked for v1.7.8 or later.

**4. Calibration step: SKIPPED.** v1.7.6 ran a budget calibration. v1.7.7's metric switch has no parameter to sweep — `last-4` is pre-committed in v1.7.6 escalation prose. The C2 sanity preflight (Task 4) replaces calibration as the discrimination check.

**5. Default backward-compat.** Existing callers running `node run.mjs --adapter hippo --n-seeds 20` without `--restrict-late-to` see ZERO behavior change. New `restrictLateTo` field appears in JSON output as `null` for backward-compat (or omitted entirely — plan picks "always present, value can be null" for schema stability).

**6. `run.mjs` made import-safe BEFORE adding exports (post-review P0-1).** `benchmarks/sequential-learning/run.mjs:591` currently calls `main().catch(...)` unconditionally at module load. Adding any `export` to this file would cause every test that imports `hitRateByPhase` or `parseRestrictLateTo` to spawn the full benchmark (50 hippo subprocesses) as an import side-effect, breaking the test suite. Task 1 wraps `main()` in an `invokedAsScript` guard (same pattern `calibrate.mjs` already uses) BEFORE adding any exports. This is the first concrete edit — verified by smoke-test before any other code change.

**7. C2 sanity gate replaces the inherited [4%, 24%] band with an N=4 lattice-aware rule (post-review P0-3).** At N=4 with 20 paired seeds, the lateMean lattice is `k/(20×4) = k/80 ∈ {0, 1.25%, 2.5%, ..., 100%}`. The inherited band `[4%, 24%]` was calibrated to the README 14% headline measured at full-late (last 7 of 25, chronological-third), not at the N=4 lattice. v1.7.7 replaces it with a stronger discrimination check: **`mean ∈ [0.05, 0.50]` AND `≥3 distinct seeds non-zero`**. The `≥3 seeds non-zero` requirement rules out the "lone outlier" failure mode where a single seed-hit could pass the inherited band by accident. The lattice math is documented in the prereg.

## Risk register

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| **Goalposts optics on the metric switch (post-review P0-4 — hard-stop added)** | (a) v1.7.6 plan P2-4 pre-committed `--restrict-late-to last-4` as the v1.7.7 escalation BEFORE running v1.7.6 calibration. (b) The decision rule (Δ≥10pp AND lower-CI>0) is unchanged from v1.7.5/v1.7.6. (c) All three verdict templates pre-committed BEFORE eval. (d) Pre-reg framing reworded from "Why this metric switch is not p-hacking" to **"Why this metric switch is a pre-committed adaptive follow-up"** (per codex review — absolute "not p-hacking" framing was too strong for an adaptive sequence over knobs). (e) Pre-reg includes a **HARD-STOP CLAUSE**: if v1.7.7 returns NOT_SUPPORTED, the −10pp magnitude is RETRACTED from CHANGELOG/README headlines; v1.8 ships as a *new hypothesis*, not a continuation. |
| **Import-side-effect breaks tests (post-review P0-1)** | `run.mjs` calls `main()` unconditionally; adding exports without wrapping would spawn hippo subprocesses on every vitest import. Task 1 Step 1 wraps `main()` in an `invokedAsScript` guard FIRST, smoke-tests the import as no-op, then proceeds to add exports. |
| **Tie-degeneracy at N=4 lattice (post-review P1-2)** | At N=4 with heavy ties (likely if C2 saturates near 0%), `pairedPermutationCI` may emit `[0,0]` and the verdict reads as null without surfacing degeneracy. Mitigation: `computeVerdict` accepts a `tiePass` flag; degenerate when `>14/20 paired diffs are exactly 0`. On `tiePass=false`, return `NOT_SUPPORTED` with `degenerate: true` in JSON summary. Result doc emits paired-diff histogram (5-bucket 2-row markdown table). |
| **Cliff-edge cases at Δ near 10pp (post-review P1-3 + P1-4)** | Pre-committed sensitivity check: if `|Δ - 0.10| < 0.02` OR `|ciLow| < 0.02`, ALSO run exact enumeration over 2^20 ≈ 1M sign-flip combinations. If exact and Monte Carlo disagree on verdict, result doc reports both and treats as borderline. NOT_SUPPORTED template has a "within-1pp-of-threshold" branch for honest reporting. |
| **Cross-version comparability of early/mid (post-review P1-1)** | At N=4: early=11/mid=10/late=4. At N=null (chronological-third): early=9/mid=9/late=7. Early/mid memory-load differs across versions. Pre-reg locks reporting scope: "v1.7.7 reports late-phase only as comparable; early/mid/learns are informational and NOT cross-N comparable." |
| **C2 floor persists at last-4** (still saturates at 0% even on the restricted window) | C2 sanity preflight (Task 4) catches this BEFORE C3 runs. SANITY_FAIL → STOP, retarget v1.8 to adversarial categories per pre-reg. C3 not collected on SANITY_FAIL — no goal-stack data leak. |
| **Discrete bounded distribution at N=4** (per-seed late rate ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}) | Documented in pre-reg. 10k Monte Carlo permutation CI handles bounded discrete distributions; not affected by ties. Tie distribution reported alongside the CI in the result doc. |
| **C2 sanity passes but C3 also saturates at 0% (Δ=0pp)** | NOT_SUPPORTED template fires mechanically. Reports the measured Δ ± CI. The mechanism is shipped from v1.7.4; the magnitude isn't demonstrated. No further escalation. |

### Mechanical preflight script (Task 4 Step 1 — adapted from v1.7.6)

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# (a) Required files exist on disk and are committed and reachable from HEAD.
for f in docs/evals/2026-05-09-v1.7.7-goal-stack-eval-prereg.md \
         docs/evals/2026-05-09-v1.7.7-claim-inventory.md \
         benchmarks/sequential-learning/analyze-v1.7.7.mjs; do
  test -f "$f" || { echo "STOP: $f missing on disk"; exit 1; }
  sha=$(git log -n1 --pretty=%H -- "$f" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [ -n "$sha" ] || { echo "STOP: $f has no commit"; exit 1; }
  git merge-base --is-ancestor "$sha" HEAD || { echo "STOP: $f commit unreachable from HEAD"; exit 1; }
done

# (b) Pre-reg pins the workload knob value verbatim. Post-review P0-2: tightened
# regex with non-digit/end-of-line trailing assertion so `--restrict-late-to 14`
# (or 24, 34, ...) does NOT silently pass.
grep -qE "(--restrict-late-to[[:space:]]+4|last-4|last 4)([^0-9]|$)" \
  docs/evals/2026-05-09-v1.7.7-goal-stack-eval-prereg.md \
  || { echo "STOP: prereg does not pin --restrict-late-to 4"; exit 1; }

# (c) No eval result dirs already exist (would imply earlier silent run).
for d in v1.7.7-eval-C0-none v1.7.7-eval-C1-static v1.7.7-eval-C2-hippo-base v1.7.7-eval-C3-hippo-goalstack; do
  test ! -e "benchmarks/sequential-learning/results/$d" \
    || { echo "STOP: $d already exists; eval would not be a fresh run"; exit 1; }
done

# (d) Working tree clean (allow pre-existing untracked).
[ -z "$(git status --porcelain | grep -v 'settings.local\|stateful-frontier')" ] \
  || { echo "STOP: working tree dirty"; exit 1; }

# (e) Post-review P1-5: analyzer + slice-math tests pass before eval runs. A
# commit that broke `computeVerdict` or `hitRateByPhase` would otherwise pass
# preflight on the strength of file-existence alone.
npx vitest run tests/sl-analyze-v1.7.7.test.ts tests/sl-restrict-late-to.test.ts --reporter=basic \
  || { echo "STOP: analyzer or slice-math tests failing"; exit 1; }

echo "PREFLIGHT OK: prereg pinned --restrict-late-to 4, no stale eval dirs, clean tree, analyzer + slice tests pass."
```

**Step 3: Update `hitRateByPhase` signature in run.mjs**

Edit `benchmarks/sequential-learning/run.mjs:309-329`:

```javascript
/**
 * Split trap results into phases and compute hit rate for each.
 *
 * v1.7.7: when `restrictLateTo` is null (default), late = last third of traps
 * (chronological third). When `restrictLateTo = N` (positive integer), late =
 * last N traps; early/mid re-split to "first ceil((total-N)/2)" / "remainder"
 * so the three slices stay disjoint and exhaustive.
 *
 * Post-review P2-2 -- `tests/agent-eval.test.ts` defines a local namesake
 * `hitRateByPhase`. If you import this module function from elsewhere, alias
 * to avoid shadowing the local in that test file.
 *
 * @param {Array<{trapCategory: string|null, trapHit: boolean}>} results
 * @param {number|null} [restrictLateTo=null] - Optional override for late slice size.
 * @returns {{early: number, mid: number, late: number}}
 */
export function hitRateByPhase(results, restrictLateTo = null) {
  const trapTasks = results.filter((r) => r.trapCategory !== null);
  const n = trapTasks.length;

  const rate = (slice) => {
    if (slice.length === 0) return 0;
    return slice.filter((r) => r.trapHit).length / slice.length;
  };

  if (restrictLateTo === null) {
    // Default: chronological third (v1.7.0..v1.7.6 behavior).
    const third = Math.ceil(n / 3);
    return {
      early: rate(trapTasks.slice(0, third)),
      mid: rate(trapTasks.slice(third, third * 2)),
      late: rate(trapTasks.slice(third * 2)),
    };
  }

  // v1.7.7: late = last N. early = first ceil((n-N)/2). mid = remainder.
  const N = Math.max(0, Math.min(restrictLateTo, n));
  const earlyEnd = Math.ceil((n - N) / 2);
  const midEnd = n - N;
  return {
    early: rate(trapTasks.slice(0, earlyEnd)),
    mid: rate(trapTasks.slice(earlyEnd, midEnd)),
    late: rate(trapTasks.slice(midEnd)),
  };
}
```

Note: `hitRateByPhase` is now `export`ed for the test. Verify no other callers in the codebase break (it was previously module-private).

**Step 4: Add `parseRestrictLateTo` helper + export**

Add near `parseArgs`:

```javascript
/**
 * Parse and validate the --restrict-late-to flag value. Returns null if input
 * is the literal string 'null' (programmatic CLI authors). Otherwise expects a
 * non-negative integer; throws otherwise.
 *
 * @param {string} raw
 * @returns {number}
 */
export function parseRestrictLateTo(raw) {
  if (typeof raw !== 'string') {
    throw new Error(`--restrict-late-to expects a string; got ${typeof raw}`);
  }
  if (!/^\d+$/.test(raw)) {
    throw new Error(`--restrict-late-to expects a non-negative integer; got "${raw}"`);
  }
  return parseInt(raw, 10);
}
```

```javascript
function parseArgs() {
  const args = process.argv.slice(2);
  const opts = {
    adapter: 'all',
    output: join(__dirname, 'results'),
    useGoalStack: false,
    evalStrict: false,
    seed: undefined,
    nSeeds: 1,
    budget: 2000,
    restrictLateTo: null, // v1.7.7 -- null preserves chronological-third behavior.
  };

  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
    if (args[i] === '--adapter' && args[i + 1]) {
      opts.adapter = args[++i];
    } else if (args[i] === '--output' && args[i + 1]) {
      opts.output = args[++i];
    } else if (args[i] === '--use-goal-stack') {
      opts.useGoalStack = true;
    } else if (args[i] === '--eval-strict') {
      opts.evalStrict = true;
    } else if (args[i] === '--seed' && args[i + 1]) {
      opts.seed = parseInt(args[++i], 10);
    } else if (args[i] === '--n-seeds' && args[i + 1]) {
      opts.nSeeds = parseInt(args[++i], 10);
    } else if (args[i] === '--budget' && args[i + 1]) {
      opts.budget = parseInt(args[++i], 10);
    } else if (args[i] === '--restrict-late-to' && args[i + 1]) {
      // v1.7.7 -- narrow the late-phase metric to last N trap encounters.
      opts.restrictLateTo = parseRestrictLateTo(args[++i]);
    } else if (args[i] === '--help' || args[i] === '-h') {
      console.log(/* ...help text... */);
      process.exit(0);
    }
  }

  return opts;
}
