```markdown
# v1.7.7 Goal-Stack Eval — Pre-Registration

**Pre-registered:** 2026-05-09, BEFORE running the eval.
**Author:** Keith So
**Mechanism under test:** B3 dlPFC goal-stack boost (`applyGoalStackBoost`), shipped v1.7.4.
**Workload variant:** default budget (2000) with `--restrict-late-to 4` — late-phase metric narrowed from "last third (7 of 25)" to "last 4 of 25 trap encounters". Single-line workload tweak preserving the metric definition shift as the only knob.
**Public-surface status of the claim:** the −10pp magnitude was untestable in v1.7.5 (floor effect on full late = last 7) and untested in v1.7.6 (budget reduction confirmed not discriminating). v1.7.7 tests on the restricted late window; result is "supported / not supported", published with measured numbers + CIs either way.

## Hypothesis

H₁: Activating the dlPFC goal-stack boost on top of base hippo reduces late-phase trap-hit-rate by ≥10 percentage points on the v1.7.7 restricted-late workload (`--budget 2000 --restrict-late-to 4`), with 95% CI lower bound > 0pp.

H₀: Activation produces no detectable improvement (95% CI for Δ overlaps 0).

## Why this metric switch is a pre-committed adaptive follow-up (post-review P0-4)

The escalation was pre-committed in the v1.7.6 plan (commit `c670ac9`, "Plan v2 — Why budget reduction, not the other 4 v1.7.5 candidates"):

> Pre-committed escalation order:
> - If v1.7.6 SANITY_FAILs → v1.7.7 will be `--restrict-late-to last-4` (deterministic, single-line workload tweak).
> - If v1.7.7 also fails → v1.8 explores adversarial trap categories (requires new lesson authoring).
> - LongMemEval R@5 corpus is a separate eval line, not a substitute.

v1.7.6 SANITY_FAILed on calibration. v1.7.7 acts on the pre-committed next step. The metric value `4` was named in the v1.7.6 escalation prose BEFORE running the v1.7.6 calibration — so this is not a result-conditional choice.

**This is a pre-committed adaptive follow-up, not p-hacking.** The chain (v1.7.5 → v1.7.6 → v1.7.7) is an adaptive sequence over workload knobs, with each individual knob pre-registered before its eval ran. The decision rule (Δ ≥ 10pp AND lower-CI > 0pp) is unchanged from v1.7.5 and v1.7.6. The seed range (0..19) is unchanged. The four-condition design is unchanged. The metric switch is the only knob in v1.7.7. The C2 sanity band changes because the N=4 lattice required recalibration (see "Sanity gate" below).

## Hard-stop clause (post-review P0-4 — retraction at NOT_SUPPORTED)

If v1.7.7 returns NOT_SUPPORTED, **the −10pp magnitude is RETRACTED from CHANGELOG / README headlines**. v1.8 (adversarial trap categories) ships as a *new hypothesis*, not a continuation of this one. The cumulative evidence after v1.7.5 saturated, v1.7.6 found B*=NULL, and v1.7.7 found Δ < 10pp is sufficient to retire the magnitude claim. The mechanism (B3 dlPFC goal-stack boost) remains shipped from v1.7.4 with no specific magnitude attached — that does not change.

## Reporting scope (post-review P1-1 — cross-version comparability lock)

v1.7.7 reports **late-phase only as the comparable metric**. Early/mid are recorded for audit but are NOT comparable to v1.7.5/v1.7.6 due to the slice re-split:

- v1.7.5 chronological-third: early=9 / mid=9 / late=7 trap encounters.
- v1.7.7 restrict-late-to=4: early=11 / mid=10 / late=4 trap encounters.

Early-phase memory load is 22% larger at N=4 than at the default. **Do not cross-cite early/mid across versions.** "Learns?" boolean is also informational only.

## Protocol

- Benchmark: `benchmarks/sequential-learning` (v1.7.5 multi-seed harness).
- **Workload knob:** `--budget 2000` (default), `--restrict-late-to 4`.
- **Conditions (4):** C0 none, C1 static, C2 hippo-base (`--use-goal-stack` OFF), C3 hippo+goalstack (`--use-goal-stack` ON).
- **Hypothesis seeds: 20.** Hash-derived in `run.mjs` (`Math.imul(0x9E3779B9, 1000+i) >>> 0` for i in 0..19) — same as v1.7.5/v1.7.6.
- **Eval mode:** `--eval-strict`.
- **Primary metric:** late-phase trap-hit-rate over the LAST 4 trap encounters per seed. Slice math (Option A from the plan): late = trapTasks.slice(21..25), early = trapTasks.slice(0..11), mid = trapTasks.slice(11..21). Disjoint and exhaustive.
- **Top-5 cap interaction:** unchanged from v1.7.5 — a task is "trap hit" iff `isRecalled(top5, category) === false`.

## Statistical method (PRE-LOCKED, unchanged primary + new sensitivity check)

- Estimand: mean late-phase Δ in pp = `mean_late(C2) − mean_late(C3)` over 20 paired seeds (positive Δ = goal-stack helped).
- **Primary CI:** 10,000 Monte Carlo resamples of paired sign-flip permutation (`pairedPermutationCI` in `aggregate.mjs`). NOT t-test — phase rates are bounded discrete.
- **Sensitivity check (POST-REVIEW P1-3, PRE-COMMITTED):** If `|Δ - 0.10| < 0.02` OR `|ciLow| < 0.02`, ALSO run **exact enumeration over 2^20 ≈ 1M sign-flip combinations** (computationally cheap; preserves cliff-edge analysis). If exact and Monte Carlo disagree on the verdict, the result doc reports BOTH and treats the result as borderline.
- **Tie-degeneracy guard (POST-REVIEW P1-2, PRE-COMMITTED):** Compute `tiePass = (count of zero paired diffs) / 20 ≤ 0.70`. If `tiePass=false` (>14 of 20 paired diffs are zero), `computeVerdict` returns `NOT_SUPPORTED` with `degenerate: true` in the structured JSON summary. The result doc flags this with: "CI is degenerate due to ties; permutation test underpowered at N=4 lattice."
- **Discrete-distribution caveat:** at N=4 trap encounters per seed, per-seed late rate ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}. Aggregate `lateMean = k/(20×4) = k/80 ∈ {0, 1.25%, 2.5%, ..., 100%}`. Result doc reports a 2-row markdown histogram (rows: C2, C3; columns: 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%; cells: count of 20 seeds at that lattice value).

## Decision rule (mechanical)

Compute Δ and 95% permutation CI on Δ.

- **Δ ≥ 0.10 AND lower-CI > 0** → **HYPOTHESIS SUPPORTED.** Ship "SUPPORTED" template citing the measured Δ, CI, and per-condition phase rates.
- **Δ < 0.10 OR CI overlaps 0** → **HYPOTHESIS NOT SUPPORTED.** Ship "NOT SUPPORTED" template. The −10pp magnitude was not demonstrated; the mechanism is shipped (v1.7.4); the hypothesis is unsupported.
- **Δ < 0 with upper-CI < 0** = goal-stack measurably HARMS performance → flag for v1.8 design review.

## Stop conditions (mid-run)

- **C2 sanity gate (post-v1.7.6 P0-2 + post-review P0-3 recalibrated for N=4 lattice):** after C2 completes, apply this stricter rule: `mean ∈ [0.05, 0.50]` AND `≥3 distinct seeds non-zero`. If FAIL, **STOP**. Do NOT run C3. Apply SANITY_FAIL template. Retarget to v1.8 adversarial categories per pre-committed escalation. C3 (goal-stack ON) is NOT collected on SANITY_FAIL — no goal-stack data leak.

  *Lattice math:* per-seed late rate at N=4 lives on `{0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}`. Aggregate over 20 seeds: `lateMean = k/(20×4) = k/80`. The inherited `[4%, 24%]` band (calibrated from a README 14% headline measured at full-late=last 7) is replaced because (a) the band is meaningless on the N=4 lattice (the 4% lower bound corresponds to ~3 hits across all 80 seed-slots, easily satisfied by a single high-rate seed); (b) `[0.05, 0.50]` is a wider headroom band that ensures discrimination room for a ≥10pp drop; (c) the `≥3 distinct seeds non-zero` requirement rules out the lone-outlier failure mode.

- **Hook failure gate (post-C3):** if `C3.hookFailures.push > 0` OR `.complete > 0`, run is contaminated. STOP, fix root cause, restart C3 with fresh result dir.
- **Seed crash policy:** drop the seed across ALL conditions (paired); replacement seed indexed 1020+. No cherry-picking.
- **Outlier policy:** any single seed >3σ from the rest in either condition → investigate and document in result doc.

## Pre-committed v1.8 escalation constraints (POST-REVIEW P1-8)

If v1.7.7 returns SANITY_FAIL or NOT_SUPPORTED, v1.8 ships adversarial trap categories with these PRE-COMMITTED constraints (named here BEFORE running v1.7.7):

- **At least 3 new trap categories** beyond the existing 10 (TRAP_CATEGORIES in `traps.mjs`).
- **Lessons must use vocabulary that has <40% Jaccard overlap with v1.7.5 lessons** (BM25 should NOT trivially match).
- **Target C2 band: `mean ∈ [0.05, 0.50]` AND `≥3 distinct seeds non-zero`** (same rule as v1.7.7 — pre-committed discrimination check, not a README-headline match).
- **Same C2-before-C3 sanity preflight rule** (no goal-stack data collected on SANITY_FAIL).
- **Categories must be authored BEFORE running C3** (no choosing-after-seeing-results).
- **All 4 conditions × 20 seeds**, hash-derived as before.

This pre-commitment exists so v1.8 cannot be retroactively justified by v1.7.7's results.
```

**Step 3: Refactor verdict computation into a pure exported `computeVerdict`**

Add near the top of the file (after imports):

```javascript
/**
 * Pure verdict computation. No I/O. Testable in isolation.
 *
 * Post-review P1-2: `tiePass` flag handles tie-degeneracy at N=4 lattice.
 * When >14 of 20 paired diffs are exactly 0 (`tiePass=false`), the permutation
 * CI is underpowered; verdict is mechanically NOT_SUPPORTED with `degenerate`
 * flag in the structured JSON summary. Caller is responsible for computing
 * `tiePass` from the paired-diff array and passing it in.
 *
 * @param {{c2Late:number, c3Late:number, delta:number, ciLow:number, ciHigh:number,
 *          hookFailures:{push:number, complete:number}|null,
 *          sanityPass:boolean,
 *          tiePass:boolean}} input
 * @returns {'SUPPORTED' | 'NOT_SUPPORTED' | 'SANITY_FAIL' | 'HOOK_FAIL'}
 */
export function computeVerdict({ c2Late, c3Late, delta, ciLow, ciHigh, hookFailures, sanityPass, tiePass }) {
  if (!sanityPass) return 'SANITY_FAIL';
  if ((hookFailures?.push ?? 0) > 0 || (hookFailures?.complete ?? 0) > 0) return 'HOOK_FAIL';
  if (tiePass === false) return 'NOT_SUPPORTED'; // degenerate, surface in result doc
  if (delta >= 0.10 && ciLow > 0) return 'SUPPORTED';
  return 'NOT_SUPPORTED';
}
```

Replace the inline verdict-derivation logic in the analyzer body with a single call to `computeVerdict({...})`. The analyzer's main body is responsible for:

1. Computing `tiePass` from the paired-diff array: `const zeroDiffCount = pairedDiffs.filter(d => d === 0).length; const tiePass = zeroDiffCount / pairedDiffs.length <= 0.70;`
2. Building the paired-diff histogram (5-bucket: 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) for both C2 and C3.
3. Calling `computeVerdict` and emitting `verdict`, `degenerate`, and `tiePass` in the JSON summary.
4. If `|delta - 0.10| < 0.02` OR `|ciLow| < 0.02`, ALSO run exact enumeration (post-review P1-3 sensitivity check) — see "exact-enumeration helper" sub-step below.

### Exact-enumeration helper (sub-step for P1-3 sensitivity)

Add to `analyze-v1.7.7.mjs`:

```javascript
/**
 * Exact paired sign-flip enumeration over 2^n combinations. For n=20 this is
 * 2^20 ≈ 1M, computable in <1s. Returns the same {ciLow, ciHigh, deltaMean}
 * shape as `pairedPermutationCI` for direct comparison. Used only when the
 * Monte Carlo result is within 2pp of a decision boundary (post-review P1-3).
 *
 * @param {number[]} c2 - per-seed C2 late rates
 * @param {number[]} c3 - per-seed C3 late rates
 * @param {number} alpha - 0.05 for 95% CI
 * @returns {{deltaMean:number, ciLow:number, ciHigh:number, exact:true}}
 */
export function exactPairedPermutationCI(c2, c3, alpha = 0.05) {
  if (c2.length !== c3.length) throw new Error('c2/c3 length mismatch');
  const n = c2.length;
  if (n > 22) throw new Error(`exact enumeration impractical for n=${n} (2^n > 4M)`);
  const diffs = c2.map((v, i) => v - c3[i]);
  const observed = diffs.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / n;
  const allMeans = [];
  const total = 1 << n; // 2^n
  for (let mask = 0; mask < total; mask++) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      sum += (mask & (1 << i)) ? -diffs[i] : diffs[i];
    }
    allMeans.push(sum / n);
  }
  allMeans.sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const meanOfNull = allMeans.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / total;
  const loIdx = Math.floor(total * (alpha / 2));
  const hiIdx = Math.ceil(total * (1 - alpha / 2)) - 1;
  return {
    deltaMean: observed,
    ciLow: observed + (allMeans[loIdx] - meanOfNull),
    ciHigh: observed + (allMeans[hiIdx] - meanOfNull),
    exact: true,
  };
}
```

If exact enumeration's verdict differs from Monte Carlo's, the result doc reports both and treats the result as borderline (per pre-reg "Statistical method").

**Step 4: Write `tests/sl-analyze-v1.7.7.test.ts`**

```typescript
// tests/sl-analyze-v1.7.7.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { computeVerdict } from '../benchmarks/sequential-learning/analyze-v1.7.7.mjs';

describe('v1.7.7 computeVerdict', () => {
  it('returns SUPPORTED when delta >= 0.10 AND ciLow > 0 AND sanity passes AND tiePass', () => {
    expect(computeVerdict({
      c2Late: 0.18, c3Late: 0.05, delta: 0.13,
      ciLow: 0.04, ciHigh: 0.22,
      hookFailures: { push: 0, complete: 0 }, sanityPass: true,
      tiePass: true,
    })).toBe('SUPPORTED');
  });

  it('returns NOT_SUPPORTED when delta < 0.10', () => {
    expect(computeVerdict({
      c2Late: 0.18, c3Late: 0.13, delta: 0.05,
      ciLow: 0.01, ciHigh: 0.09,
      hookFailures: { push: 0, complete: 0 }, sanityPass: true,
      tiePass: true,
    })).toBe('NOT_SUPPORTED');
  });

  it('returns NOT_SUPPORTED when ciLow <= 0 even if delta >= 0.10', () => {
    expect(computeVerdict({
      c2Late: 0.18, c3Late: 0.05, delta: 0.13,
      ciLow: -0.02, ciHigh: 0.28,
      hookFailures: { push: 0, complete: 0 }, sanityPass: true,
      tiePass: true,
    })).toBe('NOT_SUPPORTED');
  });

  it('returns SANITY_FAIL when sanityPass is false (overrides everything)', () => {
    expect(computeVerdict({
      c2Late: 0.0, c3Late: 0.0, delta: 0.0,
      ciLow: 0.0, ciHigh: 0.0,
      hookFailures: { push: 0, complete: 0 }, sanityPass: false,
      tiePass: true,
    })).toBe('SANITY_FAIL');
  });

  it('returns HOOK_FAIL when sanity passes but hook failures > 0', () => {
    expect(computeVerdict({
      c2Late: 0.18, c3Late: 0.05, delta: 0.13,
      ciLow: 0.04, ciHigh: 0.22,
      hookFailures: { push: 1, complete: 0 }, sanityPass: true,
      tiePass: true,
    })).toBe('HOOK_FAIL');
  });

  // Post-review P1-2 — tie-degeneracy guard
  it('returns NOT_SUPPORTED when tiePass=false even if delta >= 0.10 AND ciLow > 0', () => {
    expect(computeVerdict({
      c2Late: 0.18, c3Late: 0.05, delta: 0.13,
      ciLow: 0.04, ciHigh: 0.22,
      hookFailures: { push: 0, complete: 0 }, sanityPass: true,
      tiePass: false, // degenerate
    })).toBe('NOT_SUPPORTED');
  });
});
```

**Step 3: C2 sanity check (post-review P0-3 — N=4 lattice gate + P1-6 starvation warning)**

```bash
node --import tsx/esm -e "
  import('node:fs').then(async ({readFileSync, readdirSync}) => {
    const path = await import('node:path');
    const dir = 'benchmarks/sequential-learning/results/v1.7.7-eval-C2-hippo-base';
    const files = readdirSync(dir).filter(f => f.endsWith('.json') && f !== 'latest.json').sort();
    const j = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(dir, files[files.length - 1]), 'utf-8'));
    const condName = Object.keys(j.conditions)[0];
    const seeds = j.conditions[condName].seeds;
    const lateRates = seeds.map(r => r.phases.late);
    const m = lateRates.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/lateRates.length;
    const distinctNonZero = new Set(lateRates.filter(r => r > 0)).size; // distinct lattice values, not seed count
    const seedNonZeroCount = lateRates.filter(r => r > 0).length;
    // POST-REVIEW P0-3: N=4 lattice-aware gate.
    const inBand = m >= 0.05 && m <= 0.50 && seedNonZeroCount >= 3;
    console.log('C2 late: mean=' + (m*100).toFixed(2) + '%, seeds non-zero=' + seedNonZeroCount + '/20, distinct lattice values non-zero=' + distinctNonZero);
    console.log('Sanity gate (POST-REVIEW P0-3): ' + (inBand ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL') + ' (mean ∈ [5%, 50%] AND ≥3 seeds non-zero)');
    console.log('Per-seed late rates:', lateRates.map(r => (r*100).toFixed(0) + '%').join(', '));
    // POST-REVIEW P1-6: inline starvation warning -- if all 3 phases are zero across all 20 seeds, the adapter may be starved.
    const allPhasesZero = seeds.every(s => s.phases.late === 0 && s.phases.mid === 0 && s.phases.early === 0);
    if (allPhasesZero) {
      console.error('WARN: all phases zero across all seeds — possible adapter starvation, not just late-phase floor. Investigate before proceeding.');
    }
    if (!inBand) {
      console.error('STOP: C2 sanity FAIL. C3 will NOT be collected. Apply Task 6 SANITY_FAIL branch.');
      process.exit(1);
    }
  });
" || { echo "C2 sanity FAILED — STOP. Skip Task 5 (C3 + analyzer). Apply SANITY_FAIL branch in Task 6."; exit 1; }
```

# v1.7.9 — Retract −10pp Goal-Stack Lift Claim Implementation Plan

Source: https://github.com/kitfunso/hippo-memory/blob/master/docs/plans/2026-05-09-v1.7.9-retract-10pp-claim.md

# v1.7.9 — Retract −10pp Goal-Stack Lift Claim Implementation Plan

> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

**Goal:** Pre-emptively retract the "−10pp goal-stack late-phase trap-rate lift" magnitude claim across every public surface in the hippo-memory repo (README hero + benchmark page + benchmarks subdir READMEs + CHANGELOG retroactive entries + ROADMAP-RESEARCH + RESEARCH + TODOS + v1.7.5/6/7 eval result docs + b3-dlpfc-depth plan + GitHub Release notes for v0.11.0/v0.39.0/v1.7.4/v1.7.5/v1.7.6/v1.7.7), based on cumulative evidence from three pre-registered workload variants (v1.7.5 SANITY_FAIL, v1.7.6 B*=NULL, v1.7.7 SANITY_FAIL). Decouple retraction from v1.8.0 outcome. Pin a `docs/RETRACTION.md` magnitude-smuggling guard for v1.8. Fold in 3 of 4 P2 polish items deferred from v1.7.8 audit (P2-1 Float64Array deferred to v1.7.10 per outside voice).

**Architecture:** Doc-only release plus 3 small code/doc-polish items (P2-2/3/4). The mechanism (dlPFC goal-stack: `pushGoal`/`completeGoal` hooks, `--use-goal-stack`, `applyGoalStackBoost`, MCP/HTTP integration) remains shipped from v1.7.4. The benchmark harness (`--restrict-late-to`, `--budget`, `--eval-strict`, `analyze-v1.7.7.mjs`, `aggregate.mjs::pairedPermutationCI`) remains shipped. v1.8.0 (queued separately, not in this release) explores adversarial trap categories as **mechanism characterisation** (NOT magnitude defense), under the constraints in `docs/RETRACTION.md` shipped this release.

**Tech Stack:** Markdown edits, version bump in 5 manifests, `npm publish`, `gh release create` + `gh release edit` × 6 (retroactive append-only retraction notes on prior tags).

**Semver decision:** 1.7.9 patch because (a) no API surface change, (b) no behavior change in shipped code (P2-2/3/4 are rounding + comment + docstring; P2-1 Float64Array — the only behavior change — is deferred to v1.7.10), (c) the magnitude claim was prose-only, never in machine-readable schema. Alternative `1.8.0-retraction` rejected: 1.8.0 is reserved for the adversarial-categories release; bumping to 1.8.0 here would force renaming the queued release.

---

## Why pre-emptive retraction (deliberate departure from v1.7.7 pre-reg)

The v1.7.7 prereg and `CHANGELOG.md:41-43` read: "The hard-stop retraction clause fires on NOT_SUPPORTED, not SANITY_FAIL — v1.7.7 was SANITY_FAIL. If v1.8 also fails, the magnitude claim should be treated as falsified."

That wording made retraction conditional on v1.8 outcome. v1.7.9 retracts EARLIER. Reasoning (must appear in the v1.7.9 CHANGELOG entry verbatim):

1. **Cumulative evidence is informative without v1.8.** Three pre-registered workload variants tested across distinct knobs (saturation, budget, restricted-window). Every C2 hippo-base late mean returned 0% across every seed.

2. **The v1.7.7 prereg explicitly distinguished SANITY_FAIL (no retraction) from NOT_SUPPORTED (retraction).** v1.7.9 deviates from that distinction on cumulative-evidence grounds. The deviation is declared, not silent.

3. **The original prereg's distinction was wrong.** Three SANITY_FAILs across distinct workload knobs is meaningful negative evidence regardless of formal verdict label. v1.7.9 corrects that prereg design choice. (This is not "more conservative than the pre-reg required" — it is a different choice that prioritises public-surface honesty over completing the full pre-registered escalation chain.)

4. **Decoupling protects against v1.8 timing.** v1.8 is multi-hour eval work with new category authoring + harness tweaks. If v1.8 slips, the false magnitude claim should not stay live in the README and ROADMAP-RESEARCH.

5. **CLAUDE.md "Honest Reporting" requires it.** "If results are null, flat, or worse than the baseline, say so plainly. Do not soften, frame around it, or lead with the one positive metric." Three nulls across three pre-registered variants IS a null. The mechanism stays shipped; the magnitude is a separate claim. v1.8 still runs as planned; the retraction is independent of v1.8 outcome.

This departure is documented explicitly in the v1.7.9 CHANGELOG entry. It is NOT silent or selective retraction.

---

## Cumulative evidence (the basis for retraction)

| Release | Workload knob | Seeds | C2 hippo-base late mean | Verdict | C3 collected? |
|---------|---------------|-------|--------------------------|---------|----------------|
| v1.7.5 | full-late = last 7 of 25 (chronological-third) | 20 | 0.0% (all 20 at 0%) | SANITY_FAIL — saturation | YES (also 0.0%) |
| v1.7.6 | budget sweep {200, 400, 600, 800, 1000} | 10 each | 0.0% (all 50 single-seed runs) | B*=NULL | NO (no B* to use) |
| v1.7.7 | `--restrict-late-to 4` (last 4 of 25) | 20 | 0.0% (k=0 hits across 80 seed-slots) | SANITY_FAIL — N=4 lattice gate | NO (sanity preflight blocked C3) |

Original v0.39 informal eval reported "78% → 14%" over 50 tasks. That magnitude does not reproduce on the formal sequential-learning benchmark across three pre-registered workload variants.

---

## What gets retracted

- Headline "−10pp goal-stack lift on sequential-learning benchmark"
- "78% → 14% over 50 tasks" reproducibility framing across README, benchmarks READMEs, RESEARCH, ROADMAP-RESEARCH, CHANGELOG historical entries
- B3 success criterion "sequential-learning trap-rate −10pp" in `ROADMAP-RESEARCH.md:156`
- All marketing/thesis lines citing the magnitude (`README.md:39` hero bullet; `ROADMAP-RESEARCH.md:28` thesis line)
- Any phrasing that implies a measured magnitude. Replacement language: **"is RETRACTED. The mechanism is shipped; no magnitude is currently claimed."** No "pending", no "unsupported pending", no "untested on a discriminating workload" framing — those read as escape hatches.

## What does NOT get retracted

- The mechanism: `pushGoal` / `completeGoal` hooks, `--use-goal-stack`, `applyGoalStackBoost`, MCP/HTTP integration — all from v1.7.4..v1.7.5, all working as designed.
- The benchmark itself: harness, multi-seed variance, paired permutation CI, lattice gate framework — all working as designed.
- The infrastructure shipped in v1.7.5..v1.7.8 (adapter contract, calibration, `--restrict-late-to`, audit fixes).
- The B3 line item — it continues into v1.8.0 as adversarial-categories **mechanism characterisation** with a magnitude-smuggling guard (`docs/RETRACTION.md`, shipped this release).

## Task 5b: Pin `docs/RETRACTION.md` magnitude-smuggling guard

**Files:**
- Create: `docs/RETRACTION.md`

**Step 1: Write the file**

```markdown
# Retraction & magnitude-smuggling guard

This doc pins the v1.7.9 retraction of the "−10pp goal-stack late-phase trap-rate lift" magnitude claim and is the guard for any future release (especially v1.8.0 adversarial trap categories) against re-asserting a retracted magnitude under a different name.

## What was retracted

The v0.11.0 informal "78% → 14% over 50 tasks" headline did not reproduce on the formal sequential-learning benchmark across three pre-registered workload variants (v1.7.5 full-late SANITY_FAIL, v1.7.6 budget sweep B*=NULL, v1.7.7 `--restrict-late-to 4` SANITY_FAIL). C2 hippo-base late mean = 0.0% across every seed in every variant.

**The magnitude is RETRACTED. The mechanism is shipped; no magnitude is currently claimed.** See `CHANGELOG.md` v1.7.9 entry for the full retraction.

## What this guards against

Re-asserting the retracted magnitude under a different name. Specifically, any of the following in a future result doc, README, CHANGELOG, RESEARCH/ROADMAP-RESEARCH update, or marketing copy:

- `Δ = ` followed by a percentage-point number on late-phase trap rate
- `Xpp lift`, `Xpp drop`, `≥Xpp`, `−Xpp`, `+Xpp`
- "magnitude" applied to the goal-stack mechanism's effect on trap rate
- A pre-registered numeric pass/fail threshold on a single trap-rate metric
- "Lift" or "improvement" applied to the goal-stack mechanism without explicit "this is workload-validity, not magnitude" framing

## What this does NOT guard against

Legitimate workload-validity gates and discrimination checks are explicitly allowed:

- The N-lattice gate (`mean ∈ [0.05, 0.50]` AND ≥3 distinct seeds non-zero) IS a discrimination check on workload validity. It is not a magnitude claim about the mechanism.
- Per-seed rate reporting on individual conditions (C2, C3) for descriptive purposes.
- Hook failure counts.
- On/off comparisons that report whether the mechanism produced detectable behavioral differences (rather than asserting a specific magnitude).

## Workflow for v1.8 and beyond

Any v1.8.0+ result doc, CHANGELOG entry, or README update touching the sequential-learning benchmark MUST:

1. Reference this `docs/RETRACTION.md`.
2. State explicitly: "This release does not re-assert the retracted −10pp magnitude."
3. If reporting any number that could be read as a magnitude lift, frame it as workload-validity or descriptive characterisation, not as a mechanism-magnitude claim.
4. Pass an outside-voice review on whether the framing satisfies the guard. The v1.7.9 ship chain established this pattern; future releases inherit it.

## When this guard sunsets

This guard sunsets if and only if a future eval produces a discriminating workload (C2 hippo-base late mean within the N-lattice gate band) AND a properly pre-registered hypothesis test at that workload returns SUPPORTED with paired CI lower bound > 0. Until then, the magnitude is retracted, and any future release must satisfy this guard.

## Related documents

- `CHANGELOG.md` v1.7.9 entry (top of file)
- `docs/evals/2026-05-09-v1.7.9-retraction-inventory.md` (literal grep anchor + retraction targets)
- `docs/evals/2026-05-09-v1.7.7-goal-stack-eval-result.md` (last formal eval before retraction)
- `docs/evals/2026-05-09-v1.7.7-goal-stack-eval-prereg.md` (the prereg whose SANITY_FAIL ≠ NOT_SUPPORTED distinction v1.7.9 corrects)
- `README.md` "What's new in v1.7.9" section
- `ROADMAP-RESEARCH.md:158` v1.7.9 status update block
```

**Step 2: Commit**

```bash
git -C C:/Users/skf_s/hippo add docs/RETRACTION.md
git -C C:/Users/skf_s/hippo commit -m "docs: pin RETRACTION.md magnitude-smuggling guard for v1.8+ (v1.7.9)"
```

## Task 8: P2-3 — `pairedPermutationCI` docstring tightening

**Files:**
- Modify: `benchmarks/sequential-learning/aggregate.mjs::pairedPermutationCI`

**Step 1: Read current docstring**

**Step 2: Replace docstring with tightened version**

```javascript
/**
 * Paired permutation CI via recentred-percentile sign-flip Monte Carlo.
 *
 * Implementation: 10,000 (default) sign-flip resamples of paired diffs.
 * For each resample, multiply each diff by ±1 (random sign), compute the mean,
 * then read the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the resampled-mean distribution.
 *
 * Reports a recentred-percentile interval, NOT bias-corrected (BCa) — sufficient
 * for the symmetric, bounded paired diffs in this benchmark.
 *
 * For n < 5, returns {ciLow: 0, ciHigh: 0} as a guard against unstable tails on
 * tiny samples; callers must check this case explicitly. Larger n (n >= 10)
 * produces a usable t-band-equivalent interval.
 *
 * @param {number[]} pairedDiffs - paired (treatment - control) values.
 * @param {number} [resamples=10000] - Monte Carlo iterations.
 * @returns {{mean: number, ciLow: number, ciHigh: number, n: number}}
 */
```

## Decision log

This plan deliberately departs from the v1.7.7 pre-reg in one specific way: it triggers retraction BEFORE v1.8 runs, on cumulative evidence rather than a single NOT_SUPPORTED verdict.

**Justification (committed in plan + CHANGELOG):**
1. Three nulls across three pre-registered workload knobs is informative without v1.8.
2. The v1.7.7 prereg's SANITY_FAIL ≠ NOT_SUPPORTED distinction was wrong: three SANITY_FAILs across distinct knobs is meaningful negative evidence.
3. Decoupling protects against v1.8 timing slip.
4. CLAUDE.md "Honest Reporting" requires plain framing of nulls; v1.7.7 framing ("pending", "untested on a discriminating workload") was an escape hatch.
5. v1.8 still runs as planned; retraction is independent of v1.8 outcome.

**What this plan does NOT do:**
- Does NOT retract the mechanism (still shipped).
- Does NOT retract the benchmark (still shipped).
- Does NOT cancel v1.8 (queued, reframed as mechanism characterisation under `docs/RETRACTION.md` guard).
- Does NOT silently delete or memory-hole the original 78%→14% numbers (preserved in `git log v0.11.0` + historical CHANGELOG entry; NOT in rendered HTML).

**Outside voice resolutions (to be appended after Task 13 Step 5):**
- Pre-execution outside voice (Task 0, run 2026-05-09): senior-code-reviewer × 2 (in-house + adversarial). 27 consolidated findings; all P0 + most P1 accepted; P1 G1 (Float64Array deferral) accepted. Full disposition table to be appended at Task 13 Step 5.
- Pre-publish outside voice (Task 12): senior-code-reviewer on staged diff. P0/P1 findings block /publish-repo.

# v1.8.0 — Adversarial Trap Categories Implementation Plan

Source: https://github.com/kitfunso/hippo-memory/blob/master/docs/plans/2026-05-09-v1.8.0-adversarial-categories.md

# v1.8.0 — Adversarial Trap Categories Implementation Plan

> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

**Goal:** Characterise dlPFC goal-stack mechanism behaviour on **adversarial trap categories** (≥3 new categories with lesson vocabulary at <0.30 Jaccard overlap vs the existing 10 v1.5 categories), under the v1.7.7 prereg's pre-committed escalation constraints AND the v1.7.9 `docs/RETRACTION.md` magnitude-smuggling guard. **NO magnitude claim, NO pre-registered ≥Xpp threshold, NO pass/fail decision rule on a magnitude.** Pure mechanism characterisation: report **(a)** workload-validity sanity verdict (PASS/FAIL on `mean ∈ [0.05, 0.50] AND ≥3 distinct seeds non-zero`), **(b)** C3 per-seed lattice histogram on the adversarial-late slice, **(c)** sign-only seed-pair direction count vs C2 (k of 20 seeds where C3 strictly lower / strictly higher / tied). Anything else in the result doc is forbidden by RETRACTION.md.

**Architecture:** Add 3 new adversarial trap categories to `benchmarks/sequential-learning/traps.mjs::TRAP_CATEGORIES` (10 → 13). Each has tags + lessons + recall queries with novel vocabulary that BM25 will NOT trivially match against the recall query. Expand the 50-task workload to 62 tasks. New trap-encounter positions distributed **uniformly across early/mid/late regions** (2 each at positions 11, 21, 33, 41, 51, 59) — NOT clustered in late. Preserve `--restrict-late-to 4` as the late-phase metric (preserves the v1.7.7 N=4 lattice gate as a workload-validity check). Run C0/C1/C2/C3 × 20 seeds × `--eval-strict`. Apply C2-before-C3 sanity preflight using the same `mean ∈ [0.05, 0.50] AND ≥3 distinct seeds non-zero` rule (now framed as a workload-validity / non-saturation check, NOT a magnitude criterion per `docs/RETRACTION.md`).

**Tech Stack:** Node.js 22.5+ (existing harness), Markdown for prereg / inventory / result docs, Vitest for unit tests on Jaccard helper + new category schema + BM25-mismatch sim. No new dependencies.

**Semver decision:** 1.8.0 (minor) because the trap-category set is a public benchmark surface — going from 10 → 13 categories changes the workload definition. v1.7.x already prefigured this with the "Deferred to v1.8.0" lines in v1.7.5/6/7 CHANGELOGs. Numerical values in machine-readable schema (`benchmarks/sequential-learning/results/...json`) gain three new keys.

---

## RETRACTION.md compliance (MANDATORY — read first)

This release operates under the v1.7.9 magnitude-smuggling guard at `docs/RETRACTION.md`. Every output artifact in this plan MUST satisfy:

1. **Reference `docs/RETRACTION.md`** in the prereg, the result doc, the CHANGELOG entry, and the README "What's new in v1.8.0" block.
2. **State explicitly: "This release does not re-assert the retracted −10pp magnitude."** Verbatim, in each artifact above.
3. **No magnitude framing in any new prose.** Forbidden: `Δ\s*=`, `\b\d+pp`, `−\d+pp`, "Xpp lift", "Xpp drop", "Xpp reduction", "Xpp improvement", "lift" without workload-validity framing, "discriminating", "discrimination", "discrimination room", "magnitude" applied to mechanism effect, "median paired diff" in pp units, "5-number summary" on paired-diff distributions in pp units, side-by-side per-condition late-mean reporting that invites mental subtraction (e.g. "C2_LATE = X, C3_LATE = Y" in adjacent lines).
4. **Replacement language (use verbatim):** "non-saturation check" (replaces "discrimination check"), "non-zero variance across seeds" (replaces "discrimination room"), "C3 per-seed lattice histogram" (replaces magnitude reporting), "sign-only seed-pair direction count" (replaces paired-diff median or 5-number summary), "characterise" with operational definition (see "Operational definition" below).
5. **Outside-voice review on whether framing satisfies the guard** before /publish-repo. Same as v1.7.9 Task 12: a senior-code-reviewer pass against the staged diff. Magnitude grep regex: `(Δ\s*=|\b\d+\s*pp|−\d+pp|magnitude|discriminating|discrimination)`. Allowlist: lines containing the word `retracted` within 10 chars of the match are LEGITIMATE retraction citations and do NOT count as findings.

### Operational definition of "characterise" (NEW per outside voice D2)

For v1.8 specifically, "characterise the mechanism" means producing exactly these three reports:

1. **Sanity verdict (PASS/FAIL).** From the C2 sanity preflight at `mean ∈ [0.05, 0.50] AND ≥3 distinct seeds non-zero`. This is a workload-validity / non-saturation check. NOT a magnitude criterion.
2. **C3 per-seed lattice histogram.** For the 20 seeds, count how many landed at each lattice value `{0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}`. Report the histogram counts. NOT a magnitude — a frequency distribution over discrete values.
3. **Sign-only seed-pair direction count vs C2.** For each of 20 paired seeds, classify (C3 vs C2) as one of: `STRICTLY_LOWER` (C3 < C2), `STRICTLY_HIGHER` (C3 > C2), `TIED` (C3 = C2). Report the three counts. NOT a magnitude — direction without amplitude.

ANY other report (pp values, deltas, medians, means juxtaposed, "improvement", "reduction") is forbidden by RETRACTION.md.

## Workload size + slice math

| Quantity | v1.7.5/6/7 (existing 10) | v1.8 (10 + 3) |
|----------|---------------------------|---------------|
| Total trap categories | 10 | 13 |
| Total trap encounters per seed | 25 | 31 (existing 25 + new 6) |
| Total tasks per seed | 50 | 62 |
| Late-phase metric | `--restrict-late-to 4` (last 4 of 25 trap encounters) | `--restrict-late-to 4` (last 4 of 31 trap encounters) |
| Late-phase lattice | per-seed ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0} | unchanged (still N=4) |
| Aggregate `lateMean` | `k/(20×4) = k/80` | unchanged |
| Sanity gate | `mean ∈ [0.05, 0.50] AND ≥3 seeds non-zero` | unchanged (workload-validity / non-saturation check) |

The N=4 lattice math is preserved end-to-end. The sanity gate values are reused verbatim. Only the workload's category space changes.

**New-category position assignment (UNIFORM distribution per outside voice B2):** the 6 new trap encounters are placed at positions 11, 21, 33, 41, 51, 59 — distributed uniformly across the 62-task sequence (2 per region of early/mid/late roughly defined as 1-22, 22-42, 42-62). All 6 positions are odd (clean in v1.7.x). **NOT clustered in the late region.** With this distribution, the last-4 trap encounters (positions 48, 50, 51, 59) include 2 existing categories + 2 adversarial categories — **late-4 is mixed, not pure-adversarial.** Density math: positions 50-62 contain 1 existing trap (position 50) + 2 new (positions 51, 59) = 3 traps in 13 slots = 23% density (lower than the existing-region 50% — consistent with "no late-clustering").

| Region (62-task) | Positions | Existing traps | New traps | Total density |
|-------------------|-----------|------------------|-----------|----------------|
| Early (1-22) | 22 slots | 11 (positions 2-22 even) | 2 (positions 11, 21) | 13/22 = 59% |
| Mid (22-42) | 20 slots | 10 (positions 24-42 even) | 2 (positions 33, 41) | 12/20 = 60% |
| Late (42-62) | 20 slots | 4 (positions 44, 46, 48, 50) | 2 (positions 51, 59) | 6/20 = 30% |

(Late region has lower density by design — preserves enough clean tasks for the 12 new clean descriptions in 51-62.)

## What the result is allowed to say (and not say) — REWRITTEN per outside voice A1, A2, A4, D2

### Allowed (descriptive characterisation only, per the operational definition above)

- **Sanity verdict (PASS/FAIL).** One word. Plus a one-sentence justification: "C2 hippo-base lateMean = X, k of 20 seeds non-zero" (X is a lattice rate, NOT pp).
- **C3 per-seed lattice histogram.** Counts at each of {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}. Reported as a 5-cell histogram. Read-only on adversarial-late-slice.
- **Sign-only seed-pair direction count.** k_lower / k_higher / k_tied (sums to 20).
- **Hook-failure count** (validity check).
- **Tie-degeneracy `tiePass` boolean** (informational only).
- **Reproducibility anchors** (versions, SHAs, timestamps).

### Two-section result structure (no juxtaposition — per outside voice A1)

The result.md MUST separate condition reporting into TWO non-adjacent sections:

**Section "Workload baseline" (C0, C1, C2 only):**
- C0 none: late mean = X (95% CI ± Y) — workload no-memory baseline.
- C1 static: late mean = X (95% CI ± Y) — pre-loaded memory baseline.
- C2 hippo-base: late mean = X (95% CI ± Y) — sanity-gate input.

**Section "C3 mechanism characterisation" (C3 only, READ ONLY IF C2 sanity passed):**
- C3 per-seed lattice histogram: |0=k0|0.25=k1|0.5=k2|0.75=k3|1.0=k4| (sums to 20).
- Sign-only seed-pair direction count (vs C2): STRICTLY_LOWER=N, STRICTLY_HIGHER=N, TIED=N.
- Hook failures: push=N, complete=N.
- Tie degeneracy: tiePass=true|false.

Each section MUST contain the verbatim sentence: "Do not subtract across sections. Per `docs/RETRACTION.md`, magnitude differences between conditions are not reported in this release."

### Forbidden (per RETRACTION.md, hardened)

- `Δ = X pp` framing.
- `Xpp lift` / `Xpp drop` / `Xpp reduction` / `Xpp improvement` — even if measured.
- Median paired diff in pp units.

## Task 2: Verify <0.30 Jaccard overlap (TIGHTENED from 0.40 per outside voice E1)

**Files:**
- Create: `tools/jaccard-overlap.mjs` (one-off verification script; lives in `tools/`, not `benchmarks/`, since it's not part of the runner)
- Create: `tools/jaccard-overlap.test.ts` (unit test for the script's logic)
- Output: `docs/evals/2026-05-09-v1.8.0-jaccard-verification.txt` (committed audit artifact)

**Step 1: Define Jaccard overlap pre-registered method (extended per outside voice E1)**

For each new lesson L_new and each existing lesson L_existing:
- Tokenise: lowercase, split on `\W+`, drop stop-words, drop tokens ≤2 chars, **apply Porter-stem step** (treat "verify"/"verifying"/"verified" as the same stem `verifi`).
- **Extended stop-word set** (vs v1 draft):
  ```
  Common: a, the, an, is, are, was, were, be, been, being, of, in, on, at, to, for, with, from, by, as, and, or, not, no, do, does, did, will, would, should, could, can, may, must, this, that, these, those, it, its, has, have, had
  Modal/aux: shall, might, ought
  Engineering function words: use, uses, used, using, make, makes, made, get, gets, got, set, sets, run, runs, ran, run, find, finds, found, see, saw, seen, give, gives, gave, given, take, takes, took, taken
  ```
- Token set (after stem): `S_new = unique stems`, similarly `S_existing`.
- Jaccard = `|S_new ∩ S_existing| / |S_new ∪ S_existing|`.

Constraint: max Jaccard across all (3 × 10 = 30) pairs < **0.30** (TIGHTENED from 0.40 per outside voice E1).

**Justification for 0.30 threshold (per outside voice E1):** v1.7.7 prereg's 0.40 was an inherited default; tightening to 0.30 makes the adversarial claim stronger. With Porter-stem + extended stop-words, achievable thresholds drop ~5-10pp because stems collapse plurals/tenses; 0.30 post-stem is approximately equivalent to 0.40 pre-stem on the same lesson texts. This is documented in the prereg.

**Step 2: Implement the script**

```javascript
// tools/jaccard-overlap.mjs
import { TRAP_CATEGORIES } from '../benchmarks/sequential-learning/traps.mjs';

const STOP_WORDS = new Set([
  'a', 'the', 'an', 'is', 'are', 'was', 'were', 'be', 'been', 'being',
  'of', 'in', 'on', 'at', 'to', 'for', 'with', 'from', 'by', 'as',
  'and', 'or', 'not', 'no', 'do', 'does', 'did', 'will', 'would', 'should',
  'could', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'might', 'ought',
  'this', 'that', 'these', 'those', 'it', 'its', 'has', 'have', 'had',
  'use', 'uses', 'used', 'using', 'make', 'makes', 'made', 'get', 'gets',
  'got', 'set', 'sets', 'run', 'runs', 'ran', 'find', 'finds', 'found',
  'see', 'saw', 'seen', 'give', 'gives', 'gave', 'given', 'take', 'takes',
  'took', 'taken',
]);

// Minimal Porter-style stem: strip common verb/noun suffixes.
function stem(word) {
  return word
    .replace(/ies$/, 'y')
    .replace(/(ing|ed|es|s)$/, '')
    .replace(/(tion|ment|ness|ity|sion)$/, '');
}

export function tokenize(text) {
  return new Set(
    text
      .toLowerCase()
      .split(/\W+/)
      .filter((w) => w.length > 2 && !STOP_WORDS.has(w))
      .map(stem)
  );
}

export function jaccard(setA, setB) {
  const intersection = [...setA].filter((x) => setB.has(x)).length;
  const union = new Set([...setA, ...setB]).size;
  return union === 0 ? 0 : intersection / union;
}

const NEW_CATEGORY_IDS = ['timezone_naive', 'idempotency_retry', 'float_accumulation'];
const newCategories = TRAP_CATEGORIES.filter((c) => NEW_CATEGORY_IDS.includes(c.id));
const existingCategories = TRAP_CATEGORIES.filter((c) => !NEW_CATEGORY_IDS.includes(c.id));

let maxJaccard = 0;
let maxPair = '';

for (const newCat of newCategories) {
  const newTokens = tokenize(newCat.lesson);
  for (const existing of existingCategories) {
    const existingTokens = tokenize(existing.lesson);
    const j = jaccard(newTokens, existingTokens);
    console.log(`${newCat.id} ↔ ${existing.id}: Jaccard = ${j.toFixed(4)} (${[...newTokens].length}/${[...existingTokens].length} stems, ∩ = ${[...newTokens].filter((x) => existingTokens.has(x)).length})`);
    if (j > maxJaccard) {
      maxJaccard = j;
      maxPair = `${newCat.id} ↔ ${existing.id}`;
    }
  }
}

console.log('---');
console.log(`MAX Jaccard: ${maxJaccard.toFixed(4)} (${maxPair})`);
console.log(`THRESHOLD: 0.30 (TIGHTENED from 0.40 per outside voice E1)`);
console.log(`PASS: ${maxJaccard < 0.30 ? 'YES' : 'NO'}`);
process.exit(maxJaccard < 0.30 ? 0 : 1);
```

**Step 3: Run + capture output**

```bash

echo "Exit: $?"
```

**Expected:** exit code 0, max Jaccard < 0.30. **If FAIL** (max ≥ 0.30): rewrite the offending lesson(s) in Task 1 with more divergent vocabulary, re-run, until pass. Each rewrite attempt logs to the iteration log.

**Step 4: Unit test**

```javascript
// tools/jaccard-overlap.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { tokenize, jaccard } from '../tools/jaccard-overlap.mjs';

describe('jaccard-overlap', () => {
  it('tokenize drops stop-words, short tokens, applies Porter-style stem', () => {
    const tokens = tokenize('The quickly running fox is fast and verifies retries.');
    // 'quickly'->'quick', 'running'->'runn', 'fox', 'fast', 'verifies'->'verifi', 'retries'->'retri'
    // 'the'/'is'/'and' dropped as stop-words
    expect(tokens.has('fox')).toBe(true);
    expect(tokens.has('fast')).toBe(true);
    expect(tokens.has('the')).toBe(false);
    expect(tokens.has('and')).toBe(false);
  });

  it('jaccard of identical sets is 1', () => {
    expect(jaccard(new Set(['a', 'b']), new Set(['a', 'b']))).toBe(1);
  });

  it('jaccard of disjoint sets is 0', () => {
    expect(jaccard(new Set(['a', 'b']), new Set(['c', 'd']))).toBe(0);
  });

  it('jaccard handles partial overlap', () => {
    expect(jaccard(new Set(['a', 'b', 'c']), new Set(['b', 'c', 'd']))).toBe(0.5);
  });

  it('jaccard of two empty sets is 0 (degenerate)', () => {
    expect(jaccard(new Set(), new Set())).toBe(0);
  });

  it('Porter-stem collapses plurals/tenses', () => {
    const a = tokenize('verifies retries running');
    const b = tokenize('verify retry run');
    // Both should produce identical stems after suffix-strip.
    expect([...a].sort()).toEqual([...b].sort());
  });
});
```

```bash
git -C C:/Users/skf_s/hippo commit -m "tools(benchmark): jaccard-overlap with Porter-stem, threshold <0.30 (v1.8.0)"
```

## Task 3: BM25-mismatch sim test (NEW per outside voice E4 + B4)

**Files:**
- Create: `tests/sl-bm25-mismatch.test.ts`

**Goal:** independently verify that the new lessons are NOT trivially BM25-matched by the existing-10 recall queries (and vice versa). This is a complement to the Jaccard check — Jaccard catches lexical overlap; BM25 sim catches token-frequency-weighted match score.

**Step 1: Implement the test**

```javascript
// tests/sl-bm25-mismatch.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { TRAP_CATEGORIES } from '../benchmarks/sequential-learning/traps.mjs';

const NEW_IDS = ['timezone_naive', 'idempotency_retry', 'float_accumulation'];

// Simple BM25-like score: shared-token count weighted by inverse frequency.
function bm25Score(query, docTokens) {
  const queryTokens = query.toLowerCase().split(/\W+/).filter((w) => w.length > 2);
  let score = 0;
  for (const qt of queryTokens) {
    if (docTokens.has(qt)) score += 1;
  }
  return score;
}

function tokenize(text) {
  return new Set(text.toLowerCase().split(/\W+/).filter((w) => w.length > 2));
}

describe('BM25-mismatch sim — adversarial categories should not be top-1 for existing recall queries', () => {
  it('each existing recall query does NOT top-1-rank a new-category lesson', () => {
    const newCats = TRAP_CATEGORIES.filter((c) => NEW_IDS.includes(c.id));
    const existingCats = TRAP_CATEGORIES.filter((c) => !NEW_IDS.includes(c.id));

    for (const ec of existingCats) {
      for (const query of ec.recallQueries) {
        const allCats = [...newCats, ...existingCats];
        const scored = allCats
          .map((c) => ({ id: c.id, score: bm25Score(query, tokenize(c.lesson)) }))
          .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score);
        const top1 = scored[0];
        // For an existing-query, the top-1 should be the existing-category whose query it is, not a new adversarial one.
        expect(NEW_IDS.includes(top1.id)).toBe(false);
      }
    }
  });

  it('each new-category recall query does NOT top-1-rank an existing-category lesson', () => {
    const newCats = TRAP_CATEGORIES.filter((c) => NEW_IDS.includes(c.id));
    const existingCats = TRAP_CATEGORIES.filter((c) => !NEW_IDS.includes(c.id));

    for (const nc of newCats) {
      for (const query of nc.recallQueries) {
        const allCats = [...newCats, ...existingCats];
        const scored = allCats
          .map((c) => ({ id: c.id, score: bm25Score(query, tokenize(c.lesson)) }))
          .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score);
        const top1 = scored[0];
        // For a new-query, the top-1 should be the new-category whose query it is, not an existing one.
        expect(NEW_IDS.includes(top1.id)).toBe(true);
      }
    }
  });
});
```

**Step 2: Run + commit**

```bash
cd C:/Users/skf_s/hippo
npx vitest run tests/sl-bm25-mismatch.test.ts
git -C C:/Users/skf_s/hippo add tests/sl-bm25-mismatch.test.ts
git -C C:/Users/skf_s/hippo commit -m "tests(benchmark): bm25-mismatch sim for adversarial categories (v1.8.0)"
```

## Task 6: Update / add tests for the expanded workload

**Files:**
- Modify: any existing test that asserts `tasks.length === 50` or `trap encounters === 25`
- Add: `tests/sl-traps-v1.8.test.ts` — new unit tests for 13 categories, 31 trap encounters, 62 task slots, position uniqueness, **uniform distribution invariants**, **existing-10 PRNG-stability** (per outside voice E3)

**Step 1: Search for hardcoded 50 / 25 / 10 in tests**

```bash
git -C C:/Users/skf_s/hippo grep -nE "(50.{0,5}task|25.{0,5}trap|10.{0,5}categor)" -- tests/
```

For each hit, decide: parameterise (preferred), update to 62/31/13 (if v1.8-specific), or leave (if v1.7.7-historical and snapshot-locked).

**Step 2: New tests (TIGHTENED per outside voice B3, B2, E3)**

```javascript
// tests/sl-traps-v1.8.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { TRAP_CATEGORIES, TRAP_PLACEMENTS, generateTasks } from '../benchmarks/sequential-learning/traps.mjs';

describe('v1.8 adversarial traps', () => {
  it('has 13 trap categories (10 + 3 adversarial)', () => {
    expect(TRAP_CATEGORIES.length).toBe(13);
  });

  it('includes the 3 new adversarial categories', () => {
    const ids = TRAP_CATEGORIES.map((c) => c.id);
    expect(ids).toContain('timezone_naive');
    expect(ids).toContain('idempotency_retry');
    expect(ids).toContain('float_accumulation');
  });

  it('total trap encounters = 31', () => {
    const total = TRAP_PLACEMENTS.reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.positions.length, 0);
    expect(total).toBe(31);
  });

  it('all positions unique across categories', () => {
    const allPositions = TRAP_PLACEMENTS.flatMap((p) => p.positions);
    expect(new Set(allPositions).size).toBe(allPositions.length);
  });

  // TIGHTENED per outside voice B3: exact counts, not >=
  it('new categories have EXACTLY 6 trap positions, distributed uniformly across 62-task sequence', () => {
    const newCats = ['timezone_naive', 'idempotency_retry', 'float_accumulation'];
    const newPositions = TRAP_PLACEMENTS
      .filter((p) => newCats.includes(p.category))
      .flatMap((p) => p.positions);

    expect(newPositions.length).toBe(6);

    // Per outside voice B2: uniform distribution = ~2 per region
    const earlyCount = newPositions.filter((pos) => pos >= 1 && pos <= 22).length;
    const midCount = newPositions.filter((pos) => pos >= 23 && pos <= 42).length;
    const lateCount = newPositions.filter((pos) => pos >= 43 && pos <= 62).length;

    expect(earlyCount).toBe(2);
    expect(midCount).toBe(2);
    expect(lateCount).toBe(2);
  });

  // EXACT positions (NOT clustered in late, per outside voice B2)
  it('new positions are exactly {11, 21, 33, 41, 51, 59}', () => {
    const newCats = ['timezone_naive', 'idempotency_retry', 'float_accumulation'];
    const newPositions = TRAP_PLACEMENTS
      .filter((p) => newCats.includes(p.category))
      .flatMap((p) => p.positions)
      .sort((a, b) => a - b);
    expect(newPositions).toEqual([11, 21, 33, 41, 51, 59]);
  });

  it('generateTasks(seed=0) produces 62 tasks with 31 trap encounters', () => {
    const tasks = generateTasks(0);
    expect(tasks.length).toBe(62);
    const trapTasks = tasks.filter((t) => t.trapCategory);
    expect(trapTasks.length).toBe(31);
  });

  it('generateTasks is deterministic for fixed seed', () => {
    const a = generateTasks(42).map((t) => t.trapCategory ?? null);
    const b = generateTasks(42).map((t) => t.trapCategory ?? null);
    expect(a).toEqual(b);
  });

  it('generateTasks(seed=0) and (seed=1) produce different category-to-slot mappings', () => {
    const a = generateTasks(0).map((t) => t.trapCategory ?? null);
    const b = generateTasks(1).map((t) => t.trapCategory ?? null);
    expect(a).not.toEqual(b);
  });

  // NEW per outside voice E3: existing-10 subset PRNG-stability across workload sizes.
  // If we ever cross-cite v1.7.5/6/7 results for the existing-10 subset (we won't in v1.8,
  // per the subset-reporting lock — but document explicitly that we COULDN'T even if we wanted to).
  it('existing-10 subset placement is PRNG-stable when workload grows 50 -> 62', () => {
    // Document: this test asserts that the existing-10 categories' positions in v1.8 are
    // exactly the v1.7.x positions [2, 4, ..., 50]. The PRNG state INSIDE the new categories'
    // slot-assignment may differ, so per-position content is NOT comparable across versions.
    // The subset-reporting lock in the prereg forbids cross-version cite anyway.
    const existingIds = TRAP_CATEGORIES.filter((c) =>
      !['timezone_naive', 'idempotency_retry', 'float_accumulation'].includes(c.id)
    ).map((c) => c.id);
    const existingPlacements = TRAP_PLACEMENTS.filter((p) => existingIds.includes(p.category));
    const existingPositions = existingPlacements.flatMap((p) => p.positions).sort((a, b) => a - b);
    // Existing 25 positions, all even, in 2..50.
    expect(existingPositions.length).toBe(25);
    expect(existingPositions[0]).toBe(2);
    expect(existingPositions[24]).toBe(50);
    expect(existingPositions.every((p) => p >= 2 && p <= 50 && p % 2 === 0)).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

## Task 9: Write the result doc (descriptive characterisation, two-section format, sign-only diff reporting)

**Step 1: Compute workload baseline (C0/C1/C2) phase rates + C3 lattice histogram + sign-only direction count**

Use existing `aggregate.mjs::aggregatePhases` for per-condition phase rates. For C3 lattice histogram and sign-only direction counts, write a small script `tools/v1.8-summarise.mjs`:

```javascript
// tools/v1.8-summarise.mjs
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';

const c2 = JSON.parse(readFileSync('benchmarks/sequential-learning/results/v1.8-eval-C2-hippo-base/<latest>.json'));
const c3 = JSON.parse(readFileSync('benchmarks/sequential-learning/results/v1.8-eval-C3-hippo-goalstack/<latest>.json'));

// Per-seed late values (lattice ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0})
const c2Late = c2.seeds.map((s) => s.phases.late);
const c3Late = c3.seeds.map((s) => s.phases.late);

// C3 per-seed lattice histogram
const histogram = { 0: 0, 0.25: 0, 0.5: 0, 0.75: 0, 1.0: 0 };
for (const v of c3Late) histogram[v]++;
console.log('C3 lattice histogram:', histogram);

// Sign-only seed-pair direction count
let lower = 0, higher = 0, tied = 0;
for (let i = 0; i < c2Late.length; i++) {
  if (c3Late[i] < c2Late[i]) lower++;
  else if (c3Late[i] > c2Late[i]) higher++;
  else tied++;
}
console.log('Sign-only direction:', { STRICTLY_LOWER: lower, STRICTLY_HIGHER: higher, TIED: tied });
```

Run + capture output for the result doc.

## Decision log

This plan operates under TWO strict pre-commitment regimes:

1. **v1.7.7 prereg "Pre-committed v1.8 escalation constraints"** — 6 numbered constraints inherited verbatim and mapped to plan tasks.
2. **v1.7.9 `docs/RETRACTION.md` magnitude-smuggling guard** — descriptive characterisation framing only; sign-only diff reporting; no SUPPORTED / NOT_SUPPORTED templates; no magnitude verdicts; no median-pp; no 5-number summary in pp units; no juxtaposition; no "discriminating".

**Why these 3 adversarial categories:** vocabulary disjointness from v1.5; common real-world traps; pilot smoke test confirms at least one produces non-zero late traps for C2.

**Why uniform position distribution (not late-clustered):** late-clustering optimises for magnitude visibility, which is exactly what "characterisation only" should NOT do. Positions {11, 21, 33, 41, 51, 59} distribute new traps uniformly across early/mid/late.

**Why <0.30 Jaccard threshold (TIGHTENED from 0.40):** v1.7.7 prereg's 0.40 was an inherited default; tightening to 0.30 makes the adversarial claim stronger. Justification documented in prereg.

**What this plan does NOT do:**
- Does NOT re-assert the retracted −10pp magnitude.
- Does NOT pre-register a magnitude pass/fail decision rule.
- Does NOT use SUPPORTED / NOT_SUPPORTED templates.
- Does NOT cross-cite v1.7.5/6/7 late-phase rates as comparable to v1.8.
- Does NOT report median paired diffs, 5-number summaries on diffs, or any juxtaposed per-condition late means.
- Does NOT swap out existing 10 categories.
- Does NOT use "discriminating" / "discrimination room" / "lift" / "improvement" / "reduction" applied to the mechanism's effect.

**Outside voice questions to brief** (5 questions, answered verbatim in result.md per outside voice D3):
1. Are the 3 chosen categories sufficiently adversarial (per pilot smoke test outcome)?
2. Did uniform position distribution actually hold in the executed task generation?
3. Did the descriptive characterisation framing hold across all artifacts (prereg + inventory + result + CHANGELOG + README + RETRACTION update)?
4. Does the workload-validity verdict (PASS or FAIL) inform v1.9 direction (is LongMemEval still the right pre-committed next step)?
5. Did Task 13 staged-diff outside voice find any RETRACTION.md compliance leaks?

# v1.9.0 — LongMemEval R@5 Cross-Validation Implementation Plan (v2 — REWRITE post outside-voice)

Source: https://github.com/kitfunso/hippo-memory/blob/master/docs/plans/2026-05-09-v1.9.0-longmemeval-cross-validation.md

# v1.9.0 — LongMemEval R@5 Cross-Validation Implementation Plan (v2 — REWRITE post outside-voice)

> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

**Why this is v2:** v1 had 4 architectural P0s flagged by outside voice: (a) targeted `retrieve.py` which is explicitly NOT canonical (the file's own banner says "DO NOT compare numbers from retrieve.py against retrieve_inprocess.mjs"); (b) used a fictional `--use-goal-stack` flag that doesn't exist in hippo CLI; (c) conflated `--goal <tag>` single-tag override with the `applyGoalStackBoost` mechanism; (d) used `question_type` meta-categories as goal-tag, which would never appear as exact session tags → boost guaranteed no-op → designed-to-be-null. v2 corrects all four + 9 framing/reporting fixes.

**Goal:** Cross-validate the dlPFC `applyGoalStackBoost` mechanism (cli.ts:987-1005, fires when `sessionId && goalTag === ''`) on the LongMemEval R@5 corpus via the **canonical** `retrieve_inprocess.mjs` harness. Per-question, push a session-scoped goal with content-keyword tags extracted from the question; run recall; complete the goal. Compare C2 (goal-stack ON) vs C1 (goal-stack OFF) on the same `hippo_store`. **NO magnitude claim, NO ≥Xpp threshold, NO pass/fail decision rule on a magnitude.** Per `docs/RETRACTION.md`, mechanism characterisation only: workload-validity sanity verdict, sign-only per-question direction count (`STRICTLY_HIGHER` / `STRICTLY_LOWER` / `SAME`, NOT `STRICTLY_BETTER` / `WORSE` per outside voice B8), per-question rank-shift descriptive (operational footprint of the boost), boost-firing-rate (mechanism non-degeneracy check).

**Architecture:**
- **Harness:** `benchmarks/longmemeval/retrieve_inprocess.mjs` (canonical; in-process; budget=1M; min-results=10).
- **Mechanism path:** session-scoped `pushGoal(contentKeywordTag)` before each per-question recall; `completeGoal()` after. Drives `applyGoalStackBoost` because `sessionId !== ''` and `goalTag === ''`. NOT `--goal <tag>` override.
- **Goal-tag source:** top-K (default K=3) content-keyword stems extracted from each question via Porter-stem + extended-stop-words tokenizer (reused from v1.8's `tools/jaccard-overlap.mjs::tokenize`). Both ingest-side session-tags AND recall-side goal-tags content-derived → real token overlap structurally possible.
- **Conditions:** C1 (no goal-stack), C2 (session-scoped goal-stack via pushGoal). Both on same `hippo_store`. C0 (BM25-only) dropped from active comparison; cited prose-only with explicit "different-store provenance" caveat.
- **Workload size:** all 500 questions × 2 conditions.

**Tech Stack:** Node.js (existing `retrieve_inprocess.mjs`), Python (existing `evaluate_retrieval.py`), Vitest for new tests on the keyword-extractor + sign-only summariser. No new package dependencies.

**Semver decision:** 1.9.0 (minor). LongMemEval harness gains `--use-goal-stack` flag (in MJS, not Python) + `--goal-tag-source` flag. Additive feature; no breaking change.

## Task 1: Add `--use-goal-stack` + `--goal-tag-source` + `--max-questions` flags to `retrieve_inprocess.mjs`

**Files:**
- Modify: `benchmarks/longmemeval/retrieve_inprocess.mjs` (canonical harness)
- Create: `benchmarks/longmemeval/keyword-extractor.mjs` (content-keyword tokenizer, reused from v1.8 Jaccard tool's tokenize logic)

**Step 1: Read current `retrieve_inprocess.mjs` shape**

Already done at Task 0. Confirm flag-parsing pattern + recall-call shape.

**Step 2: Create the keyword-extractor module**

Reuse the Porter-stem + extended-stop-words tokenizer from `tools/jaccard-overlap.mjs`. Extract top-K stems by frequency (or, if all stems are unique within the question, top-K by position).

```javascript
// benchmarks/longmemeval/keyword-extractor.mjs
import { tokenize } from '../../tools/jaccard-overlap.mjs';

/**
 * Extract top-K content-keyword stems from a question.
 * Reuses v1.8 Jaccard tokenizer: lowercase, split on \W+, drop stop-words,
 * drop short tokens, Porter-stem.
 *
 * @param {string} questionText
 * @param {number} k - max stems to return (default 3)
 * @returns {string[]} stems, ordered by first-occurrence position
 */
export function extractKeywordStems(questionText, k = 3) {
  const stems = [...tokenize(questionText)];
  return stems.slice(0, k);
}
```

**Step 3: Add flags to `retrieve_inprocess.mjs::parseArgs`**

```javascript
// New flags (additive; preserve existing behaviour)
'--use-goal-stack': boolean (default false) — enable session-scoped pushGoal/completeGoal per question
'--goal-tag-source': enum (default 'question-keywords') — source for goal-tags. 'question-keywords' uses extractKeywordStems(question, 3).
'--max-questions': integer (default null) — limit to first N questions (for pilot/dev). null = all 500.
```

**Step 4: Plumb the goal-stack hooks per question**

For each question in the eval loop:

```javascript
if (opts.useGoalStack) {
  const stems = extractKeywordStems(question, 3);
  const sessionId = `lme-${question_id}`; // unique per question for isolation
  for (const stem of stems) {
    await hippoApi.pushGoal({ tenantId, sessionId, tag: stem });
  }
  // recall WITHOUT explicit goalTag (so applyGoalStackBoost fires per cli.ts:1005 gate)
  const memories = await hippoApi.recall({ query: question, sessionId, /* no goalTag */ });
  // record boost-firing flag in result
  const boostFired = memories.some((m) => m._goalBoosted === true);
  // complete the goal stack (drains the active goals so next question starts fresh)
  await hippoApi.completeGoal({ tenantId, sessionId });
  // ...
} else {
  const memories = await hippoApi.recall({ query: question /* no sessionId, no goalTag */ });
  // ...
}
```

**Note on boost-firing telemetry:** `applyGoalStackBoost` per cli.ts:990-1005 modifies the score per memory. To capture which memories were boosted, either (a) attach a `_goalBoosted` flag to the returned memory objects (requires harness modification), OR (b) infer from rank-shifts between C1 and C2 (compute post-hoc). Pick whichever is cheaper; document choice in Task 1 commit message.

**Step 5: Record per-question metadata in retrieval JSONL**

Add to each retrieval record:
- `goal_tags_pushed`: string[] (or null if --use-goal-stack=false)
- `boost_fired`: boolean (or null if telemetry path (b) chosen)
- `top_1_memory_id`: string (used for rank-shift descriptive at result-write time)

**Step 6: Tests**

```javascript
// tests/longmemeval-keyword-extractor.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { extractKeywordStems } from '../benchmarks/longmemeval/keyword-extractor.mjs';

describe('LongMemEval keyword extractor', () => {
  it('extracts top-3 content stems from a question', () => {
    const stems = extractKeywordStems('What did the user say about the meeting schedule yesterday?', 3);
    expect(stems.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(3);
    expect(stems).toContain('user'); // not stop-word
    // 'said' (verb), 'meeting', 'schedule', 'yesterday' candidates
  });

  it('respects k parameter', () => {
    const stems = extractKeywordStems('one two three four five six seven', 2);
    expect(stems.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(2);
  });

  it('returns empty array for stop-word-only input', () => {
    const stems = extractKeywordStems('a is to the and of for', 3);
    expect(stems).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('Porter-stems plurals/tenses', () => {
    const a = extractKeywordStems('users meetings schedules', 3);
    const b = extractKeywordStems('user meeting schedule', 3);
    expect(a).toEqual(b);
  });
});
```

**Step 7: Commit (Task 1 SHA = audit anchor — "goal-stack hooks added BEFORE C2 ran")**

## Decision log

This plan v2 is a deliberate rewrite after outside voice flagged 4 architectural P0s in v1. Documented:

**v1 problems (corrected):**
- Wrong harness (`retrieve.py` non-canonical) → v2 uses `retrieve_inprocess.mjs`.
- Fictional `--use-goal-stack` flag → v2 invents the flag in MJS, plumbs to actual `applyGoalStackBoost` path via session-scoped pushGoal/completeGoal.
- Conflated `--goal` single-tag override with `applyGoalStackBoost` → v2 explicitly drives the latter (sessionId set, goalTag empty).
- `question_type` meta-categories as goal-tag (designed-to-be-null) → v2 uses content-keyword stems (Porter-stem from v1.8 Jaccard tokenizer).

**v1 framing fixes (corrected):**
- Per-category breakdown leaks magnitude through clustering → v2 drops it entirely.
- Sanity gate `[0.40, 0.95]` calibrated to PASS → v2 uses `[0.55, 0.90]` AND adds boost-firing-rate non-degeneracy gate.
- C0 + C1 side-by-side invites mental subtraction → v2 reports C1 only in baseline section; C0 cited prose-only.
- "STRICTLY_BETTER" / "STRICTLY_WORSE" value-loaded → v2 uses "STRICTLY_HIGHER" / "STRICTLY_LOWER" / "SAME" matching v1.8 vocabulary.
- Cumulative-null trigger missing → v2 pre-commits the trigger BEFORE v1.9 runs.
- v1.10 = embeddings (substrate change, not mechanism fix) → v2 v1.10 = goal-tag mapping iteration; embeddings deferred to v1.11.
- C0 provenance unchecked → v2 cites with explicit "different-store provenance" caveat.

**What this plan does NOT do:**
- Does NOT re-assert the retracted −10pp magnitude.
- Does NOT pre-register a magnitude pass/fail decision rule.
- Does NOT use SUPPORTED / NOT_SUPPORTED templates.
- Does NOT use STRICTLY_BETTER / STRICTLY_WORSE terminology.
- Does NOT report per-category direction-with-attribution.
- Does NOT cross-cite v1.7.5/6/7/8 numbers as comparable to LongMemEval.
- Does NOT pre-tag sessions with question_type at ingest (would leak).

**Outside voice questions (5 named, must answer verbatim in result.md per outside voice C6):** see Task 3.

# F6 LongMemEval Reranker Hardening Implementation Plan

Source: https://github.com/kitfunso/hippo-memory/blob/master/docs/plans/2026-05-10-f6-reranker-hardening.md

# F6 LongMemEval Reranker Hardening Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Add a pluggable reranker pass to the hybrid retrieval path and characterise its effect on LongMemEval R@5 across three escalating tracks (lexical-feature, cross-encoder, LLM), under the v1.8.1 pre-registration discipline.

**Architecture:** Insert a `rerank()` step in `hybridSearch` between MMR re-ordering (`src/search.ts:534-543`) and budget filtering (`src/search.ts:545-554`). Rerankers are pluggable via a `reranker?: RerankerFn` option; default is `null` (current behaviour preserved). Three implementations land in `src/rerankers/{features,cross-encoder,llm}.ts`. The LongMemEval harness (`benchmarks/longmemeval/retrieve_inprocess.mjs`) gains a `--reranker {features|cross-encoder|llm}` flag. Tier-1 micro-eval gains paired A/B fixtures per track.

**Tech Stack:** TypeScript, vitest (real SQLite, no mocks), Python harness, optional `@xenova/transformers` for cross-encoder (already a peer dep), customer-supplied OpenAI-compatible endpoint for LLM track.

---

## Spec source

`ROADMAP-RESEARCH.md:372-374` — F6 LongMemEval reranker hardening. Roadmap text: *"Close gap from current R@5 toward MemPalace's 96.6% via reranker tuning + cross-encoder evaluation. R@5 ≥ 85% on LongMemEval with the existing hybrid path."*

**Effort:** 6d single-engineer (lane B parallel during May Wks 1-4 per ROADMAP-RESEARCH.md:461).

**Branch:** `claude/plan-implementation-workflow-sasNp` (this session). New code lands here; merges to `main` after eng-review.

---

## Retraction-discipline framing (READ FIRST)

`docs/RETRACTION.md:5-7` (added v1.8.1) requires: **no eval pre-commitment is binding without (a) source-read of the dependency code paths AND (b) a 1-question dry-run wired through the actual mechanism path that confirms the mechanism FIRES before pre-reg locks.** The magnitude-smuggling guard at `docs/RETRACTION.md:15-23` prohibits:

- "Δ = Xpp", "Xpp lift/drop"
- "Magnitude" applied to a mechanism's effect
- A pre-registered numeric pass/fail threshold on a single metric
- "Lift" / "improvement" without explicit workload-validity framing

The roadmap's "R@5 ≥ 85%" is therefore **NOT** treated as a binary pass/fail in this plan. It is a non-blocking target. The pre-registration in Task 1 frames the eval as workload-validity (does each reranker fire on ≥X% of queries; does R@5 vary across hyperparameters at all) plus descriptive characterisation across the three tracks.

Every result doc, CHANGELOG entry, and README update produced by this plan MUST contain the verbatim sentence: *"This release does not re-assert the retracted −10pp magnitude."* Per `docs/RETRACTION.md:39`.

---

**Create:**

- `src/rerankers/features.ts` — Track 1: lexical/feature reranker (uses `confidence`, `schema_fit`, `kind`, `strength`, `outcome_*`)
- `src/rerankers/cross-encoder.ts` — Track 2: MS-MARCO MiniLM cross-encoder via `@xenova/transformers`
- `src/rerankers/llm.ts` — Track 3: pairwise listwise rerank via OpenAI-compatible endpoint
- `src/rerankers/index.ts` — `getReranker(name)` factory
- `tests/rerankers/features.test.ts`
- `tests/rerankers/cross-encoder.test.ts`
- `tests/rerankers/llm.test.ts`
- `tests/rerankers/integration-hybrid-search.test.ts` — integration via `hybridSearch({ reranker })`
- `benchmarks/micro/fixtures/reranker_features.json`
- `benchmarks/micro/fixtures/reranker_cross_encoder.json`
- `benchmarks/longmemeval/run_reranker_sweep.mjs` — orchestrator that runs the harness across all three tracks + baseline
- `docs/evals/2026-05-10-f6-reranker-prereg.md` — pre-registration document (with dry-run evidence)
- `docs/evals/2026-05-10-f6-reranker-result.md` — result document (post-eval)

**Modify:**
- `src/search.ts:234-557` — add `reranker?: RerankerFn` option to `hybridSearch`, slot reranker call between MMR and budget filtering
- `src/search.ts:165-225` — extend `SearchResult.breakdown` with optional `rerankScore`, `preRerankRank`, `postRerankRank`
- `benchmarks/longmemeval/retrieve_inprocess.mjs:18-30` — add `--reranker`, `--reranker-config` flags
- `package.json` — add `@xenova/transformers` as optional peer dep entry if not already present (it is — confirm in Task 8)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — v1.9.0 entry after eval result lands
- `ROADMAP-RESEARCH.md:372-374` — flip F6 status from `[next]` to `[shipped]` with eval-result link

**Why split rerankers into separate files:** each reranker has independent dependencies (Track 1 = none, Track 2 = transformers, Track 3 = network). Splitting prevents unused-import bloat in CLI startup and lets each be tested in isolation. `index.ts` is the single import surface.

```bash
npm run build
node -e '
  import("./dist/search.js").then(async ({ hybridSearch, buildCorpus }) => {
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing integration test**

Create `tests/rerankers/integration-hybrid-search.test.ts`:

```typescript
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { hybridSearch, type SearchResult } from '../../src/search.js';
import { createMemory } from '../../src/memory.js';
import type { RerankerFn } from '../../src/rerankers/types.js';

describe('hybridSearch reranker seam', () => {
  it('invokes the reranker after MMR and before budget filtering', async () => {
    const entries = [
      createMemory('CI pipeline failure on push to master'),
      createMemory('Python dict ordering guarantees in 3.7+'),
      createMemory('Production database is hosted on us-east-1'),
    ];

    const calls: { query: string; resultCount: number }[] = [];
    const stub: RerankerFn = async (query, results) => {
      calls.push({ query, resultCount: results.length });
      // Reverse order to prove the reranker output replaces the input ordering
      return [...results].reverse().map((r, i) => ({
        ...r,
        rerankScore: results.length - i,
      }));
    };

    const out = await hybridSearch('CI failure', entries, {
      budget: 100000,
      reranker: stub,
    });

    expect(calls.length).toBe(1);
    expect(calls[0].query).toBe('CI failure');
    expect(calls[0].resultCount).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    // Reranker output ordering is preserved
    expect(out[0].entry.id).toBe(entries[entries.length - 1].id);
  });

  it('skips reranker when option not provided (current behaviour preserved)', async () => {
    const entries = [createMemory('the quick brown fox')];
    const out = await hybridSearch('fox', entries, { budget: 100000 });
    expect(out.length).toBe(1);
    expect(out[0]).not.toHaveProperty('rerankScore');
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `npx vitest run tests/rerankers/integration-hybrid-search.test.ts`

- [ ] **Step 3: Create the types file**

Create `src/rerankers/types.ts`:

```typescript
import type { SearchResult } from '../search.js';

/**
 * A reranker reorders (and optionally rescales) the candidate set produced
 * by hybridSearch's BM25 + cosine + MMR pipeline. Rerankers run AFTER MMR
 * de-duplication and BEFORE token-budget filtering, so the reranker sees
 * the full diversity-balanced candidate pool but does not see candidates
 * already filtered out by score-zero or supersession.
 *
 * Rerankers MUST be deterministic for a given (query, results) input
 * unless explicitly documented as stochastic (LLM track). Determinism is
 * required for paired A/B and for the workload-validity gate in
 * docs/evals/2026-05-10-f6-reranker-prereg.md.
 */
export type RerankerFn = (
  query: string,
  results: SearchResult[],
  options?: RerankerOptions,
) => Promise<RerankResult[]>;

export interface RerankerOptions {
  /** Cap candidates passed to the reranker. Default 50. */
  topK?: number;
  /** Per-track config blob; opaque to the seam. */
  config?: Record<string, unknown>;
}

export interface RerankResult extends SearchResult {
  /** Score assigned by the reranker. Replaces `score` for downstream
   *  ordering; original `score` preserved on the SearchResult. */
  rerankScore: number;
  /** 1-indexed rank in the input to the reranker. */
  preRerankRank: number;
  /** 1-indexed rank in the reranker output. */
  postRerankRank: number;
}

/**
 * Signals available to feature-based rerankers, extracted once per
 * candidate to avoid re-tokenizing or re-fetching.
 */
export interface RerankSignals {
  confidence: 'verified' | 'observed' | 'inferred' | 'stale' | null;
  schemaFit: number;
  kind: 'raw' | 'distilled' | 'superseded' | 'archived' | null;
  strength: number;
  retrievalCount: number;
  outcomePositive: number;
  outcomeNegative: number;
  emotionalValence: 'neutral' | 'error' | 'success' | 'critical' | null;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `featuresReranker`**

Create `src/rerankers/features.ts`:

```typescript
import { tokenize } from '../search.js';
import type { RerankerFn, RerankResult, RerankerOptions } from './types.js';

const CONFIDENCE_WEIGHT: Record<string, number> = {
  verified: 1.30,
  observed: 1.10,
  inferred: 0.90,
  stale: 0.70,
};

const KIND_WEIGHT: Record<string, number> = {
  distilled: 1.10,
  raw: 1.00,
  superseded: 0.50,
  archived: 0.30,
};

/**
 * Track 1 reranker: rescore the candidate set using signals already on
 * MemoryEntry. No external dependencies, no network, no model load.
 *
 * Score = base_score * confidence_w * kind_w * (0.7 + 0.3*schema_fit)
 *       * (0.8 + 0.2*tanh(strength)) * (1 + 0.1*tanh(pos-neg))
 *       * exact_overlap_boost
 *
 * Weights are calibrated for sign and order, NOT a magnitude claim.
 * See docs/plans/2026-05-10-f6-reranker-hardening.md Task 3.
 */
export const featuresReranker: RerankerFn = async (
  query,
  results,
  options?: RerankerOptions,
): Promise<RerankResult[]> => {
  const topK = options?.topK ?? 50;
  const head = results.slice(0, topK);
  const queryTerms = new Set(tokenize(query));

  const rescored = head.map((r, i) => {
    const e = r.entry;

    const confW = CONFIDENCE_WEIGHT[e.confidence ?? ''] ?? 1.0;
    const kindW = KIND_WEIGHT[e.kind ?? ''] ?? 1.0;
    const schemaFitW = 0.7 + 0.3 * (e.schema_fit ?? 0.5);
    const strengthW = 0.8 + 0.2 * Math.tanh(e.strength ?? 0);

    const pos = e.outcome_positive ?? 0;
    const neg = e.outcome_negative ?? 0;
    const outcomeW = 1 + 0.1 * Math.tanh((pos - neg) / 2);

    const docTerms = new Set(tokenize(`${e.content} ${e.tags.join(' ')}`));
    let overlap = 0;
    for (const t of queryTerms) if (docTerms.has(t)) overlap++;
    const overlapW = queryTerms.size > 0 ? 1 + 0.2 * (overlap / queryTerms.size) : 1;

    const rerankScore = r.score * confW * kindW * schemaFitW * strengthW * outcomeW * overlapW;

    return {
      ...r,
      rerankScore,
      preRerankRank: r.preRerankRank ?? i + 1,
      postRerankRank: 0,
    };
  });

  rescored.sort((a, b) => b.rerankScore - a.rerankScore);
  rescored.forEach((r, i) => (r.postRerankRank = i + 1));

  return rescored;
};
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Create the factory**

Create `src/rerankers/index.ts`:

```typescript
import { featuresReranker } from './features.js';
import type { RerankerFn } from './types.js';

const REGISTRY: Record<string, RerankerFn> = {
  features: featuresReranker,
};

export function getReranker(name: string | null | undefined): RerankerFn | null {
  if (!name) return null;
  const fn = REGISTRY[name];
  if (!fn) throw new Error(`Unknown reranker: ${name}. Available: ${Object.keys(REGISTRY).join(', ')}`);
  return fn;
}

export type { RerankerFn, RerankResult, RerankerOptions, RerankSignals } from './types.js';
```
